general_skills.title: Apply Angle Bisector Theorem for Segment Ratios
general_skills.principle: Use the Angle Bisector Theorem to determine how an angle bisector divides the opposite side in the ratio of adjacent sides, enabling segment length calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an angle bisector intersects a side of a triangle, split the side into segments proportional to the adjacent sides.

general_skills.title: Derive and Solve Algebraic Equations from Geometric Constraints
general_skills.principle: Set up equations based on geometric theorems (e.g., Stewart's Theorem) and solve for unknown lengths by algebraic manipulation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given side lengths and a geometric condition (e.g., angle bisector), derive equations to compute unknown segment or length values.

general_skills.title: Simplify Ratios Using Algebraic Expressions
general_skills.principle: Compute ratios of lengths by simplifying algebraic expressions derived from geometric relationships, ensuring consistency with given constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When required to find a ratio of segments or lengths after determining individual values through geometric or algebraic methods.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Constraint Transformation
general_skills.principle: Reframe the problem into equivalent algebraic conditions by isolating variables and identifying constraints (e.g., perfect square equations, inequalities).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a problem requiring conditions on variables (e.g., perfect squares, divisibility) and need to derive relationships between them.

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Enumeration
general_skills.principle: Iterate through possible values of a key variable (e.g., a) and count valid subcases (e.g., m) that satisfy derived constraints, ensuring no overlaps or gaps.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting solutions to a problem with discrete variables and bounded ranges, and the solution depends on partitioning the domain into manageable subsets.

general_skills.title: Fraction Simplification via Coprimality
general_skills.principle: Reduce fractions by identifying and removing common factors through prime analysis, ensuring the numerator and denominator are coprime.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After computing a fraction representing a probability or count, when simplifying it to its lowest terms using number-theoretic properties.

general_skills.title: Modular Arithmetic for Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use modular arithmetic to derive constraints on variables by analyzing residue classes under given divisibility conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires satisfying a congruence condition (e.g., sum divisible by a number) through residue assignments.

general_skills.title: Structural Grouping for Simplification
general_skills.principle: Partition elements into structured groups based on their positions or properties to decompose complex constraints into manageable subproblems.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem's conditions can be satisfied by ensuring each group meets specific, independent criteria (e.g., residue assignments per group).

general_skills.title: Symmetry Adjustment via Group Order
general_skills.principle: Divide total counts by the order of the symmetry group to account for equivalent configurations under rotational or reflective symmetries.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting distinct arrangements and rotational/reflectional symmetries are considered equivalent.

general_skills.title: Decompose Complex Expressions
general_skills.principle: Break down complicated sums into simpler components (e.g., splitting terms into separate series) to isolate manageable parts for analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a complex expression that can be split into simpler, known components.

general_skills.title: Leverage Series Identities
general_skills.principle: Use known mathematical identities (e.g., for factorial-based series) to derive closed-form expressions for sums involving factorials or exponential terms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering sums that align with standard series expansions or combinatorial identities.

general_skills.title: Apply Modular Simplification
general_skills.principle: Use properties of modular arithmetic (e.g., divisibility, congruence) to simplify large computations involving factorials or products under modular constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with problems involving large factorials or products where direct computation is infeasible, and modular properties can reduce complexity.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Setup
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric figures based on given lengths and constraints to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given a geometric configuration with specific lengths or ratios, use coordinate geometry to model the problem.

general_skills.title: Parametrize Lines and Solve for Geometric Conditions
general_skills.principle: Parametrize a line segment and solve systems of equations derived from geometric properties (e.g., parallelism) to find points satisfying trapezoid conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When identifying points on a line that satisfy specific geometric constraints, such as parallel sides in trapezoids.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Distance Calculation
general_skills.principle: Use coordinate differences and distance formulas to compute distances between points, simplifying expressions through algebraic manipulation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating distances between points derived from geometric or parametric representations.

general_skills.title: Translate geometric constraints into algebraic equations
general_skills.principle: Identify key relationships between geometric properties (e.g., tangent angles) and algebraic expressions (e.g., derivatives) to derive conditions for solving the problem.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given a geometric condition involving curves, slopes, or angles, convert it into an algebraic equation or inequality.

general_skills.title: Apply integral calculus to compute arc length
general_skills.principle: Use the arc length formula and substitution techniques to evaluate integrals, simplifying them into solvable forms through variable transformations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When computing the length of a curve defined implicitly or parametrically, set up the integral and apply substitution to resolve the integrand.

general_skills.title: Extract constants from structured expressions
general_skills.principle: Match a simplified mathematical expression to a target form (e.g., $\frac{a}{b}(c\sqrt{d}-e)$) to identify and sum individual components.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an answer must be expressed in a specific algebraic form, decompose the result into its constituent terms for final computation.

general_skills.title: Coordinate-Based Distance Calculation
general_skills.principle: Use the distance formula between integer-coordinate points to compute side lengths of polygons, leveraging algebraic properties of coordinates.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given vertices with integer coordinates and required to compute perimeter or side lengths.

general_skills.title: Vector Cross Product for Area
general_skills.principle: Compute the area of a parallelogram using the magnitude of the cross product of its adjacent side vectors, applicable to any planar figure with vector-defined sides.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the area of a parallelogram or other planar figure from vector relationships between vertices.

general_skills.title: Volume Conservation Principle
general_skills.principle: When objects can be reshaped without compression, their total volume remains constant, allowing comparison with the container's volume to determine feasibility.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves reshaping objects (e.g., melting, combining) while preserving volume, use total volume comparisons to assess container capacity.

general_skills.title: Volume Ratio for Quantity Estimation
general_skills.principle: Divide the container's volume by the object's volume to compute the maximum number of identical objects that can fit when reshaped, assuming no compression.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining how many objects (of fixed volume) can fit into a container via reshaping, calculate the ratio of container volume to object volume.

general_skills.title: Geometric Distribution Expectation
general_skills.principle: Model the expected number of trials until the first success in independent, identical trials using the geometric distribution formula $ E = \frac{1}{p} $, where $ p $ is the success probability per trial.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing scenarios with repeated independent trials and a constant success probability.

general_skills.title: Conditional Expectation with Constraints
general_skills.principle: When given a relationship between variables (e.g., $ Y = kX $), derive conditional expectations by setting up algebraic equations and simplifying using series or probability identities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving dependent or constrained variables requiring conditional probability analysis.

general_skills.title: Fraction Simplification via Factoring
general_skills.principle: Reduce fractions by factoring numerator and denominator, then verify coprimality through prime factorization or divisibility checks.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying complex fractions in number theory or algebraic contexts.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis with Constraints
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into total possibilities and invalid scenarios based on constraints, then compute each case separately.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves restrictions that require distinguishing between valid and invalid configurations.

general_skills.title: Permutation Calculation
general_skills.principle: Use permutations to count arrangements of distinct positions when order matters and no repetitions are allowed.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When assigning distinct roles or positions with unique entities and no overlaps.

general_skills.title: Subtraction Principle
general_skills.principle: Subtract invalid configurations from the total count to isolate valid solutions, especially when constraints eliminate specific cases.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints invalidate certain subsets of total possibilities, and direct counting is complex.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric figures to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations, enabling precise calculations and relations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves geometric configurations that can be represented in a coordinate system.

general_skills.title: Invariant Recognition
general_skills.principle: Derive algebraic expressions and simplify them to identify invariants or properties that hold regardless of variable parameters.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem's solution depends on a constant value or relationship that remains unchanged under varying conditions.

general_skills.title: Case Testing for Verification
general_skills.principle: Test specific cases to validate the correctness of a general solution, ensuring consistency across all possible scenarios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying the robustness of a derived formula or conclusion in problems with variable parameters.

general_skills.title: Decompose complex numbers into real and imaginary parts
general_skills.principle: Express complex numbers in terms of their real and imaginary components to isolate known and unknown variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given constraints on specific components (e.g., imaginary part) of a complex number.

general_skills.title: Solve equations via algebraic manipulation
general_skills.principle: Rearrange and simplify equations to isolate variables, leveraging algebraic identities and properties of complex numbers.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for unknowns in equations involving complex numbers or other structured mathematical objects.

general_skills.title: Equate specific components to derive constraints
general_skills.principle: Use the equality of specific components (e.g., real or imaginary parts) to form solvable equations from given conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem provides information about particular components of a mathematical entity (e.g., imaginary part of a complex number).

general_skills.title: Sum of Arithmetic Sequence
general_skills.principle: Identify sequences with a common difference and apply the formula for their sum (e.g., sum of first n odd numbers is n²).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a pattern involves incremental values with a consistent difference, such as rows increasing by 2.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Based Solution Fitting
general_skills.principle: Narrow down possible solutions by checking divisibility, range limits, or other problem-specific constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem specifies bounds (e.g., rows between 10-20) or requires divisibility conditions (e.g., equal distribution).

general_skills.title: Problem-Wording Interpretation
general_skills.principle: Determine whether phrased ranges (e.g., 'between 10 and 20') are inclusive or exclusive based on context and example cases.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When ambiguity in problem statements requires logical deduction from examples or constraints.

general_skills.title: Ratio-Based Variable Assignment
general_skills.principle: Assign variables to segments based on given ratios to decompose complex geometric configurations into manageable parts.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves proportional divisions of line segments or ratios of lengths in a geometric figure.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Law Application
general_skills.principle: Use the Law of Sines or Cosines to relate angles and sides in triangles, especially when multiple angle constraints are present.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for unknown angles or sides in triangles with known angle measures or proportional relationships.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Equation Simplification
general_skills.principle: Transform trigonometric equations into algebraic forms by isolating variables, factoring, or using identities to solve for target quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When deriving relationships between angles requires simplifying equations involving trigonometric functions or ratios.

general_skills.title: Generalize from Examples
general_skills.principle: Identify patterns in small cases and extend them to broader conclusions, ensuring consistency with the problem's constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given specific instances of a mathematical structure, use them to hypothesize a general rule or property.

general_skills.title: Derive Sequence Formulas
general_skills.principle: Express the sum of a sequence as a closed-form formula by analyzing its structure and arithmetic properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a sequence follows a linear or predictable pattern, derive a formula for its cumulative sum.

general_skills.title: Simplify Ratios for Integrality
general_skills.principle: Reduce complex expressions to simpler forms and determine conditions under which the result is an integer by analyzing divisors.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating ratios of sums or sequences, simplify algebraically and identify divisor conditions for integrality.

general_skills.title: Decompose Product into Known/Unknown Components
general_skills.principle: When given a product that includes both desired and undesired elements, identify and isolate subsets (e.g., even/odd numbers) to compute the desired part.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Use when a product spans multiple categories (e.g., even/odd, prime/composite) and the goal is to extract a specific subset.

general_skills.title: Isolate Desired Component via Division
general_skills.principle: Divide a known product by the product of known components to isolate the target quantity, leveraging algebraic relationships between factors.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a target value is embedded within a larger product and can be derived by eliminating known, extraneous factors.

general_skills.title: Extend Range by Combining Segments
general_skills.principle: Break a target range into contiguous segments, compute each segment's product separately, and combine results to derive the full product.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Use when a problem requires computing a product over a larger range by splitting it into smaller, manageable parts.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Translation
general_skills.principle: Convert verbal problem constraints into mathematical equations by defining variables and expressing relationships explicitly.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a problem requiring quantitative relationships between variables, define variables and derive equations based on the problem's conditions.

general_skills.title: Systematic Value Testing
general_skills.principle: Iterate through feasible values of discrete variables (e.g., digits) within bounds, leveraging simplifications to narrow search space and identify valid solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems with discrete, bounded variables, test values methodically using derived constraints to eliminate invalid cases.

general_skills.title: Solution Verification
general_skills.principle: Substitute candidate solutions back into the original problem to confirm they satisfy all stated conditions and edge cases.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After identifying potential solutions, verify their validity by rechecking against the problem's original requirements.

general_skills.title: Use Extremal Values for Optimization
general_skills.principle: When optimizing under constraints, consider setting variables to their domain's extremes to simplify the problem and reduce complexity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves minimizing/maximizing a function with constraints on variable ranges, especially when variables can take on boundary values.

general_skills.title: Substitute to Reduce Variables
general_skills.principle: Express multiple variables in terms of fewer parameters using constraints, then derive a single-variable function to solve for the optimal configuration.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with systems of equations derived from constraints, use substitution to isolate key variables and simplify the optimization problem.

general_skills.title: Leverage Algebraic Constraints for Optimization
general_skills.principle: Formulate equations from constraints and solve for critical points by balancing terms, ensuring the solution satisfies both the constraint and the objective function.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When minimizing/maximizing a target expression (e.g., sums of powers) under a given constraint, derive and solve equations that link the variables and their powers.

general_skills.title: Symmetry-Based Equidistant Identification
general_skills.principle: In regular polygons, the center is the unique point equidistant to all vertices due to rotational symmetry. This principle applies to any subset of vertices, as their perpendicular bisectors intersect only at the center.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing equidistant points in symmetric configurations like regular polygons or circles.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Configuration Elimination
general_skills.principle: Systematically evaluate all possible cases (e.g., triplets of vertices) and eliminate non-symmetric or invalid configurations that do not satisfy the equidistant condition, leveraging geometric properties to narrow possibilities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems requiring enumeration of unique points under symmetric constraints.

general_skills.title: Perpendicular Bisector Convergence
general_skills.principle: In regular polygons, the intersection of perpendicular bisectors of chords always occurs at the center. This ensures the center is the only point equidistant to multiple vertices in symmetric figures.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining equidistant points for subsets of vertices in regular or highly symmetric geometric structures.

general_skills.title: Solve Linear Recurrences via Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Decompose a recurrence relation into homogeneous and particular solutions, then use initial conditions to determine constants in the general solution.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a functional equation or recurrence relation can be expressed as a linear combination of terms with known forms.

general_skills.title: Apply Modular Arithmetic to Final Computations
general_skills.principle: Compute the remainder of a large value modulo a given number by simplifying the expression before evaluation, especially when the target value is derived from a closed-form formula.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires the remainder of a computed value divided by a specific integer, such as 1000.

general_skills.title: Logarithmic Equivalence to Exponentials
general_skills.principle: When multiple logarithmic expressions are equal, set them equal to a common variable and convert each to exponential form to express variables in terms of that variable.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering equations with multiple logarithmic terms set equal to each other.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Identity Simplification
general_skills.principle: When faced with equations involving exponents of different bases, substitute variables to express them in terms of common bases, then apply algebraic identities to simplify and solve.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying equations derived from exponential relationships with distinct bases.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Assignment for Geometric Configurations
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to points in a geometric figure to translate constraints into algebraic equations, simplifying complex relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves multiple intersecting lines, circles, or ratios, and coordinate geometry can reduce the problem to algebraic computations.

general_skills.title: Area-Based Dimension Inference
general_skills.principle: Use the area formula for trapezoids (or other polygons) to deduce missing dimensions, such as height or base lengths, when given partial information.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a geometric figure's area is provided alongside some side lengths, and the goal is to find unknown dimensions that complete the figure.

general_skills.title: Systematic Equation Solving for Intersections
general_skills.principle: Solve systems of equations derived from line and circle intersections to determine coordinates of key points, then compute distances or ratios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires finding intersections of lines, circles, or other curves, and algebraic methods are feasible to compute exact coordinates.

general_skills.title: Model State Transitions with Probabilities
general_skills.principle: Represent systems with discrete states and transitions between them, using probabilities to compute long-term behavior or iterative outcomes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves sequential decisions or states with probabilistic transitions between them.

general_skills.title: Apply Modular Arithmetic for Large Exponents
general_skills.principle: Use modular arithmetic to simplify computations involving large exponents, particularly when combined with division or fractions requiring modular inverses.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with problems that involve repeated operations (e.g., exponentiation) and require results modulo a number.

general_skills.title: Digit Frequency Analysis
general_skills.principle: Systematically count occurrences of each digit in specified number ranges by decomposing numbers into positional components (e.g., hundreds, tens, units) and aggregating counts across segments.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining resource requirements based on digit usage in structured numerical ranges.

general_skills.title: Maximal Demand Determination
general_skills.principle: The number of required packages equals the maximum frequency of any single digit, as each package provides one of every digit.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When resources are constrained by the availability of individual elements (e.g., digits) in fixed quantities per unit.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric figures to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations, enabling precise computation of areas and intersections.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves complex geometric configurations that can be simplified via coordinate assignments.

general_skills.title: Proportional Segments Analysis
general_skills.principle: Use given segment lengths to infer proportional relationships between parts of a figure, which can simplify calculations of ratios and intersections.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When segment divisions or extensions (e.g., AD, CF) create proportional relationships that govern the problem's structure.

general_skills.title: Area Ratio via Base/Height
general_skills.principle: Compute areas of triangles using base-height formulas, then derive ratios by comparing proportional components of these areas.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing areas of triangles sharing common bases or heights, or when areas are determined through coordinate-derived dimensions.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition in Alternating Series
general_skills.principle: Identify structural patterns in alternating sums by grouping terms and deriving closed-form expressions based on the parity of the upper limit.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with an alternating series involving powers or polynomials, analyze the sign alternation and group terms to simplify the sum.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification for Large Expressions
general_skills.principle: Break down complex multiplicative expressions into smaller, manageable components to compute results efficiently, especially for large numbers.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating products or powers in a sum, decompose them into simpler parts (e.g., distributive property) to avoid direct computation.

general_skills.title: Apply Totient Function's Multiplicative Property
general_skills.principle: When numbers are coprime, φ(ab) = φ(a)φ(b). Use this to decompose φ(36n), φ(25n), and φ(16n) into prime-power components for simplification.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When decomposing totient functions of composite numbers into their prime factorized forms.

general_skills.title: Prime Factorization for Totient Computation
general_skills.principle: Break down numbers into prime factors to compute φ(n) using the formula φ(n) = n ∏ (1 - 1/p) for distinct primes p dividing n.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing φ(n) for numbers with known or variable prime factors.

general_skills.title: Systematic Candidate Testing for Optimization
general_skills.principle: Test potential solutions in descending order of magnitude to find the largest valid value under constraints, especially when the problem requires maximizing a variable.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking the maximum or minimum value of a variable subject to a mathematical condition.

general_skills.title: Logarithmic Leading Digit Analysis
general_skills.principle: Use the fractional part of log₁₀(N) to determine the leading digit of N, leveraging the relationship between exponents and digit patterns.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing the leading digit of numbers in a sequence defined by exponentiation or logarithmic growth.

general_skills.title: Equidistribution for Count Estimation
general_skills.principle: Approximate the number of elements in a sequence satisfying a condition by assuming uniform distribution of fractional parts of logarithmic expressions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When estimating occurrences of properties (e.g., leading digits) in sequences generated by exponential functions over large ranges.

general_skills.title: Refine Estimates with Given Constraints
general_skills.principle: Adjust approximate counts based on explicit data points (e.g., known leading digits of boundary terms) to ensure accuracy in final results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem provides specific information about edge cases or boundary values that influence the exact count.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis via Ordering
general_skills.principle: When constraints involve inequalities, order the variables to reduce redundancy, e.g., assume a ≤ b ≤ c and apply the triangle inequality as a + b > c.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with problems requiring comparisons among multiple variables under inequality constraints.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Summation Simplification
general_skills.principle: Use known formulas for sums (e.g., ∑c² and ∑c) to compute large combinatorial quantities efficiently, especially when counting valid or invalid configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating totals or differences involving sequences of integers over a range.

general_skills.title: Geometric-Combinatorial Translation
general_skills.principle: Translate geometric conditions (e.g., triangle inequality) into combinatorial constraints by rephrasing them in terms of ordered variables and summations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When integrating geometric principles (e.g., distances, inequalities) into probability or counting problems involving discrete structures.

general_skills.title: Variable Substitution for System Reduction
general_skills.principle: Express variables in terms of others to simplify systems of equations, reducing the problem to fewer variables while preserving constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a system of equations involving multiple variables and constraints, substitute variables to minimize complexity.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Inequality Derivation
general_skills.principle: Apply non-negativity constraints to derive inequalities that bound variables, enabling identification of critical thresholds for parameters.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables are constrained to be non-negative, use inequalities to establish relationships between variables and parameters.

general_skills.title: Inequality Combination for Parameter Bounds
general_skills.principle: Combine derived inequalities to find necessary conditions on parameters, ensuring consistency across all constraints and minimizing/maximizing the target value.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining minimal or maximal values for a parameter, use combined inequalities to enforce compatibility between all constraints.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis by Parity
general_skills.principle: Break problems into odd/even cases to exploit distinct function behaviors and simplify recursive analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a function's definition depends on the parity of the input, split into cases to handle each branch systematically.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition for Convergence
general_skills.principle: Identify sequences (e.g., powers of 2) that monotonically reduce to the target value through consistent operations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing iterative processes, look for patterns that guarantee convergence to a desired outcome.

general_skills.title: Cycle and Divergence Elimination
general_skills.principle: Test trajectories for cycles or unbounded growth to eliminate candidates that fail to reach the target.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating paths in recursive functions, verify that sequences do not loop indefinitely or diverge to infinity.

general_skills.title: Translate Remainder Conditions into Equations
general_skills.principle: When given a number and its remainder upon division by an unknown, subtract the remainder to form a multiple of the divisor. This allows expressing the problem in terms of divisibility.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves remainders and requires finding a common divisor.

general_skills.title: Compute GCD of Adjusted Numbers
general_skills.principle: Use the Euclidean algorithm to find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of adjusted numbers derived from remainders. This identifies potential candidates for the unknown divisor.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem reduces to finding a common divisor of two adjusted values.

general_skills.title: Validate Candidates Against Original Conditions
general_skills.principle: Test each candidate divisor against the original remainder conditions to ensure it satisfies all constraints in the problem.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After identifying potential divisors via GCD, to confirm they meet the problem's specific remainder requirements.

general_skills.title: Prime Factor Decomposition for Moduli
general_skills.principle: Break down composite moduli into prime factors to solve congruences separately, leveraging the Chinese Remainder Theorem for combination.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires solving a congruence modulo a composite number, first factor the modulus into its prime components.

general_skills.title: Modular Congruence Simplification
general_skills.principle: Use properties like Euler's theorem or direct computation to reduce exponents in congruences, simplifying the search for solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with high exponents in modular arithmetic, simplify the congruence using known theorems or given conditions.

general_skills.title: Candidate Generation and Validation
general_skills.principle: Generate candidate values that satisfy individual congruence conditions and validate them against all constraints to find the minimal solution.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple modular constraints must be satisfied simultaneously, systematically test candidates that meet each condition.

general_skills.title: Factor Exponential Expressions
general_skills.principle: Break down terms with exponents into common bases to simplify complex fractions, leveraging algebraic identities like a^{m+n} = a^m * a^n.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying ratios involving large exponents with shared bases.

general_skills.title: Substitute Ratios for Simplification
general_skills.principle: Introduce a substitution (e.g., x = (a/b)^k) to transform ratios into manageable forms, enabling algebraic manipulation and estimation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with expressions involving ratios of similar terms with exponents.

general_skills.title: Bound Expressions via Small Term Estimation
general_skills.principle: Estimate the magnitude of negligible terms (e.g., x << 1) to establish bounds on expressions, determining integer parts through inequalities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing expressions where small terms dominate the behavior of the entire expression.

general_skills.title: Scale Areas via Similarity
general_skills.principle: When two figures are similar, their areas are proportional to the square of their linear scaling factor. Use this relationship to compute areas of transformed shapes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a geometric figure is scaled uniformly and similarity is confirmed.

general_skills.title: Simplify Radical Expressions
general_skills.principle: Expand and simplify expressions involving radicals by distributing terms and combining like terms, particularly when dealing with nested radicals or fractions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When algebraic manipulations involve square roots or fractional exponents.

general_skills.title: Analyze Geometric Transformations
general_skills.principle: Identify how folding, scaling, or other transformations alter geometric configurations, and use properties of regular polygons or symmetry to derive proportional relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves folding, symmetry, or transformations that create similar or related figures.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Variable Limitation
general_skills.principle: When a variable and its reciprocal are both integers, the variable must be ±1. This follows from the requirement that 1/x is an integer, which restricts x to divisors of 1.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given that a variable and its reciprocal are integers, narrow down possible values to ±1.

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Enumeration with Deduplication
general_skills.principle: Systematically generate all combinations of allowed variable values, compute the target expression for each, and collect distinct results to determine unique outcomes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables have limited options (e.g., ±1) and the target expression depends on their combinations, enumerate all possibilities and identify distinct results.

general_skills.title: Decompose Constraints into Independent Subproblems
general_skills.principle: Identify and isolate constraints that apply to distinct groups, solving each group's possibilities separately before combining results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves multiple independent constraints affecting different subsets of entities.

general_skills.title: Count Valid Pair Combinations with Constraints
general_skills.principle: For pairs with constraints (e.g., same or different items), calculate valid combinations by considering the constraint's effect on choice options.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing pairs of entities with specific relationship constraints (e.g., identical or distinct choices).

general_skills.title: Apply Multiplication Principle for Independent Choices
general_skills.principle: Multiply the number of possibilities for independent subproblems to determine the total number of valid configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When subproblems are independent, meaning the choices in one do not affect the choices in another.

general_skills.title: Angle Ratio and Triangle Sum
general_skills.principle: When given angle ratios in a triangle with a known right angle (e.g., from a diameter), use the triangle angle sum to compute individual angles.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Identify a triangle with a right angle and known angle ratios to solve for missing angles.

general_skills.title: Parallel Lines and Inscribed Angles
general_skills.principle: Use parallel lines to establish equivalent angles (e.g., alternate interior angles) and apply inscribed angle theorems to relate arcs and angles.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When parallel lines intersect chords or diameters, leverage angle equivalences to find arc measures or inscribed angles.

general_skills.title: Factor Quadratics for Simplification
general_skills.principle: Decompose complex denominators into linear factors to simplify expressions, enabling further algebraic manipulation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering polynomial denominators in sums or integrals that can be factored into simpler terms.

general_skills.title: Partial Fraction Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break rational functions into simpler fractions to transform complex expressions into manageable components.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with rational functions in sums or integrals that require decomposition into elementary terms.

general_skills.title: Telescoping Series Recognition
general_skills.principle: Identify patterns where consecutive terms cancel, allowing infinite sums to collapse to a finite value through cancellation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating infinite series that exhibit cancellation properties, such as alternating sums with recursive terms.

general_skills.title: Test Small Integers for Potential Solutions
general_skills.principle: When solving equations with integer constraints, systematically test small integer values to identify possible solutions, especially when algebraic manipulation is infeasible.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves finding integer solutions and the equation's structure does not allow for straightforward algebraic simplification.

general_skills.title: Analyze Equation Behavior Across Variable Ranges
general_skills.principle: Evaluate the equation's behavior for different ranges of variables (e.g., positive/negative, large/small values) to eliminate impossible cases based on sign, growth, or parity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the feasibility of solutions by examining how the equation's components behave across critical intervals of the variable.

general_skills.title: Logarithmic to Exponential Conversion
general_skills.principle: Translate logarithmic conditions into equivalent exponential equations to simplify the problem. For example, log_a b = k implies a^k = b, allowing direct analysis of integer solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves logarithmic conditions that can be rephrased as exponential relationships.

general_skills.title: Exponent Range Analysis
general_skills.principle: Determine valid exponents k by ensuring a^k falls within the problem's bounds. For each k, compute the maximum a such that a^k ≤ upper_bound using root operations and floor functions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing integer solutions where a^k must satisfy a range constraint, such as 2 ≤ a^k ≤ N.

general_skills.title: Systematic Counting with Floor Functions
general_skills.principle: For each exponent k, count valid bases a by computing floor(upper_bound^(1/k)) - 1, which represents the number of integers a ≥ 2 satisfying a^k ≤ upper_bound.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When enumerating integer pairs (a, k) where a^k lies within a specified range, and k is a positive integer.

general_skills.title: Parity and Prime Constraints
general_skills.principle: Analyze the parity of the target sum and properties of primes (e.g., evenness) to narrow down possible pairs. For even sums, both primes must be odd unless one is 2, which is the only even prime.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving sums of primes with a fixed total, use parity and prime properties to eliminate invalid cases.

general_skills.title: Systematic Prime Testing
general_skills.principle: Test small primes in ascending order to find the minimal valid value, ensuring the complement also satisfies the problem constraints (e.g., primality).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When searching for the smallest or largest value in a constrained set, systematically test candidates starting from the smallest or largest possible values.

general_skills.title: Symmetric Pair Summation
general_skills.principle: In problems where pairs (a, b) satisfy a + b = C, the minimal a and maximal a will sum to C, as their complements (b and a) are symmetrically related.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves symmetric pairs with a fixed sum, recognize that the minimal and maximal values of one variable will add to the total.

general_skills.title: Nested Expression Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Evaluate complex nested expressions by systematically starting from the innermost layer and working outward, ensuring each sub-expression is resolved in sequence.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with deeply nested operations that require step-by-step simplification.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition in Recursive Operations
general_skills.principle: Identify invariant patterns in recursive operations (e.g., 2x - 2) that stabilize to a fixed value, even when applied repeatedly to intermediate results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering operations that produce consistent outputs under specific transformations, regardless of intermediate values.

general_skills.title: Reciprocal Unification
general_skills.principle: When given reciprocal relationships, convert them to a common denominator to find a unified expression that simplifies the problem structure.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with quantities that involve reciprocals, such as altitudes or other inverse relationships, use common denominators to combine them into a single term.

general_skills.title: Fractional Simplification
general_skills.principle: When simplifying complex fractions, factor and cancel common terms to reduce the expression to its simplest form, preserving algebraic equivalence.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with nested or compound fractions, decompose them into prime factors and cancel shared components to streamline calculations.

general_skills.title: Formula-Driven Geometry
general_skills.principle: When geometric quantities depend on reciprocal relationships, apply derived formulas that connect the product or sum of reciprocals to the target quantity (e.g., area).
general_skills.when_to_apply: In problems involving inverse relationships (e.g., altitudes, slopes), use algebraic identities or geometric formulas that directly relate reciprocals to the desired output.

general_skills.title: Equation Translation
general_skills.principle: Translate verbal problem conditions into algebraic equations by identifying key relationships and constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves numerical relationships or constraints that can be expressed mathematically.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis and Simplification
general_skills.principle: Solve equations through algebraic manipulation and case analysis to explore all potential solutions systematically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple scenarios or variables require testing distinct cases to find valid solutions.

general_skills.title: Constraint Verification
general_skills.principle: Check solutions against problem-specific constraints (e.g., coprimality, positivity) to eliminate invalid cases.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solutions must satisfy additional conditions beyond the initial equation derivation.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Setup
general_skills.principle: Model geometric configurations using coordinates to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves complex geometric relationships that can be simplified by assigning coordinates to key points.

general_skills.title: Tangency Proportionality
general_skills.principle: Use tangency conditions to derive proportional relationships between segments in a triangle, leveraging geometric constraints like equal tangent lengths.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a semicircle or circle is tangent to two sides of a triangle, leading to ratios between side lengths.

general_skills.title: System of Equations for Lengths
general_skills.principle: Solve systems of equations derived from distance formulas to determine unknown lengths in a triangle or other geometric figures.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple distance constraints (e.g., from coordinates or side ratios) require simultaneous solving to find specific measurements.

general_skills.title: Check Coprimality via Euclidean Algorithm
general_skills.principle: To determine if a multiplicative inverse exists modulo m, compute gcd(a, m) using the Euclidean algorithm. If the gcd is 1, the inverse exists.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for a modular inverse of a number a modulo m, first verify that a and m are coprime.

general_skills.title: Apply Extended Euclidean Algorithm
general_skills.principle: Use the extended Euclidean algorithm to find integers x and y such that ax + my = 1, which directly yields the modular inverse of a modulo m.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking the modular inverse of a number a modulo m, perform the extended Euclidean algorithm on a and m.

general_skills.title: Adjust Negative Results to Modulus Range
general_skills.principle: Convert negative modular inverses to their positive equivalents by adding the modulus until the result lies in the range [0, m).
general_skills.when_to_apply: After computing a modular inverse as a negative number, adjust it to the standard positive range by adding the modulus.

general_skills.title: Model Constraints as Set Operations
general_skills.principle: Represent problem constraints as subsets of a universal set, ensuring all conditions are encoded in set intersections/uniions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints involve exclusion of specific combinations or inclusion of required subsets.

general_skills.title: Apply Inclusion-Exclusion for Overlapping Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use inclusion-exclusion to calculate valid configurations by alternately adding/subtracting overlaps of forbidden or missing conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple constraints must be satisfied simultaneously, and their overlaps need systematic adjustment.

general_skills.title: Geometric to Algebraic Modeling
general_skills.principle: Translate geometric configurations into coordinate systems and algebraic equations to derive relationships between variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a geometry problem involving lengths, reflections, or midpoints, assign coordinates and express constraints algebraically.

general_skills.title: Quadratic Constraint Analysis
general_skills.principle: Solve quadratic equations derived from geometric conditions and analyze roots to determine valid variable ranges.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems that involve squared terms or distances, derive and solve quadratic equations while checking for feasible solutions within specified intervals.

general_skills.title: Integer Solution Verification
general_skills.principle: Check for integer solutions within constraints by testing boundary conditions and ensuring derived values satisfy all problem requirements.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem specifies integer values or discrete constraints, validate solutions by verifying they meet both algebraic and geometric criteria.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Assignment for Geometry
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric figures to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When modeling problems involving shapes, distances, or angles that can be represented in a coordinate plane.

general_skills.title: Perpendicular Slope Condition
general_skills.principle: Two lines are perpendicular if the product of their slopes equals -1, enabling algebraic verification of geometric constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given conditions about perpendicularity in a coordinate or geometric context.

general_skills.title: Equation Derivation from Constraints
general_skills.principle: Formulate and solve equations derived from geometric relationships to isolate unknown quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for variables in problems involving geometric or algebraic constraints.

general_skills.title: Leverage Recursive Properties
general_skills.principle: Identify and exploit recursive relationships in sequences (e.g., τ² = τ + 1) to simplify expressions or derive closed-form formulas.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering sequences defined by recurrence relations, especially those tied to constants like the golden ratio.

general_skills.title: Use Generating Functions for Series
general_skills.principle: Apply generating functions to evaluate infinite series involving known sequences (e.g., Lucas numbers) by substituting values into their generating function expressions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a series can be expressed in terms of a known sequence's generating function, such as Lucas numbers or Fibonacci numbers.

general_skills.title: Decompose Sums into Manageable Parts
general_skills.principle: Split a sum into initial terms and a general part, compute each separately, and combine results to simplify the overall calculation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a series has distinct behaviors for small indices and a general pattern for larger indices, allowing separation of contributions.

general_skills.title: Apply Definitions to Problem Constraints
general_skills.principle: When encountering a problem involving specific mathematical properties (e.g., relatively prime numbers), start by precisely defining the required condition and aligning it with the problem's parameters.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires understanding a mathematical concept's exact criteria (e.g., GCD, divisibility, or combinatorial properties).

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Enumeration
general_skills.principle: For counting problems, methodically enumerate all possible cases by iterating through each value of one variable and determining valid outcomes for the other, ensuring no duplicates or omissions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating probabilities or counts involving discrete, finite sets (e.g., dice rolls, permutations, or integer pairs).

general_skills.title: Simplify Fractions via GCD Reduction
general_skills.principle: After computing a fraction representing a probability or ratio, reduce it to lowest terms by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor (GCD).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When finalizing answers that require expressing results as simplified fractions (e.g., in probability or number theory problems).

general_skills.title: Case Interval Evaluation
general_skills.principle: To evaluate a piecewise function, determine which interval the input falls into by systematically checking each case's condition against the input value.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a piecewise-defined function and an input value requiring case selection.

general_skills.title: Constant Position Analysis
general_skills.principle: Use known mathematical constants' approximate values to determine their position relative to function intervals, ensuring alignment with the correct case definition.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a constant (e.g., π, e) needs to be evaluated in a piecewise function requiring interval-based case selection.

general_skills.title: Factor by Recognizing Patterns
general_skills.principle: Identify algebraic identities (e.g., difference of cubes) or grouping opportunities to simplify complex polynomials into manageable factors.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a high-degree polynomial that can be decomposed via factoring techniques.

general_skills.title: Solve Quadratics via Formula
general_skills.principle: Use the quadratic formula to solve equations of the form $ ax^2 + bx + c = 0 $, especially when roots are required in specific forms like $ \frac{m + \sqrt{n}}{r} $.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a polynomial reduces to a quadratic after factoring or simplification.

general_skills.title: Validate Root Constraints
general_skills.principle: Check that parameters of a root's form (e.g., coprimality of numerator and denominator, positivity) align with problem constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After identifying a root's expression to ensure it meets specified conditions for the problem.

general_skills.title: Factor and Simplify Complex Expressions
general_skills.principle: Recognize patterns (e.g., quadratics, squares) in expressions to rewrite them into simpler forms, enabling direct analysis of minima or maxima.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a complex polynomial or expression that can be decomposed into recognizable algebraic structures.

general_skills.title: Use Calculus for Critical Point Analysis
general_skills.principle: Compute derivatives to identify critical points, evaluate the function at these points, and determine minima/maxima through local behavior analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing a differentiable function over real numbers, particularly when algebraic simplification is insufficient.

general_skills.title: Verify Minima via Non-Negative Summation
general_skills.principle: Transform the expression into a sum of non-negative terms (e.g., squares) to confirm that the minimum value is achievable and consistent with derived critical points.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After identifying critical points, use algebraic identities to validate that the minimum value is indeed attainable and correct.

general_skills.title: Identify Necessary Conditions for Target Range
general_skills.principle: Determine the minimal requirements for a target range by analyzing feasible combinations, such as recognizing that numbers between 10-20 require a '1' in the tens place.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves forming numbers within a specific range with limited digit options, identify the essential digits or values needed.

general_skills.title: Use Complementary Counting for Probability
general_skills.principle: Calculate favorable outcomes by subtracting unfavorable cases from total possibilities, such as computing (total outcomes - no-1 outcomes) to find at least-one-1 scenarios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating probabilities involving 'at least one' condition, use complementary counting to simplify the computation.

general_skills.title: Decompose sequences into periodic intervals
general_skills.principle: Identify repeating patterns (e.g., intervals between perfect squares) and break the sequence into manageable segments for analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a sequence exhibits periodic behavior defined by a mathematical rule (e.g., sign changes after squares).

general_skills.title: Apply known summation formulas for alternating series
general_skills.principle: Use established formulas for alternating sums of integers, squares, cubes, etc., to compute contributions from distinct intervals efficiently.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating sums with alternating signs that follow a structured pattern (e.g., $\sum (-1)^{m+1} m^k$).

general_skills.title: Combine interval results to compute total
general_skills.principle: Aggregate contributions from individual intervals using algebraic manipulation to derive the final value of the entire sequence.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After decomposing a complex sum into smaller, solvable components, combine their results systematically.

general_skills.title: Complete the Square for Quadratic Constraints
general_skills.principle: Transform quadratic equations into squared terms to simplify constraints and reveal geometric or algebraic relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a quadratic constraint involving multiple variables, complete the square for each variable to reduce complexity.

general_skills.title: Simplify Target Expressions via Pattern Recognition
general_skills.principle: Identify algebraic structures (e.g., perfect squares, factoring) in target expressions to rewrite them in simpler, more manageable forms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing or analyzing expressions, look for patterns like (x + y)^2 or factoring to reduce computational complexity.

general_skills.title: Substitute Parametric Relationships to Reduce Variables
general_skills.principle: Derive parametric expressions from constraints and substitute them into target functions to eliminate variables and find extrema.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a constraint defines a relationship between variables, use substitution to express the target function in terms of fewer variables.

general_skills.title: Apply Known Geometric Properties
general_skills.principle: Use established properties of regular polygons (e.g., area ratios, diagonal relationships) to shortcut complex calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves regular polygons and the solution relies on known structural or proportional relationships.

general_skills.title: Identify Structural Proportions
general_skills.principle: Recognize how specific configurations (e.g., diagonals spanning edges) partition a figure into components with predictable area ratios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing geometric figures where key components (like rectangles or triangles) have known relative areas to the whole.

general_skills.title: Apply Standard Volume Formulas
general_skills.principle: Recall and use established volume formulas for regular polyhedrons (e.g., octahedron, cuboctahedron) to compute their volumes in ratio problems.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing volumes of polyhedrons with known geometric formulas.

general_skills.title: Simplify Algebraic Ratios
general_skills.principle: Compute ratios of volumes by algebraically simplifying expressions, canceling terms, and reducing to their simplest form.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When deriving ratios between geometric quantities involving shared variables (e.g., edge length).

general_skills.title: Apply Graph Invariants for Cycle Bounds
general_skills.principle: Use the cyclomatic number (m - n + p) to determine the minimal number of cycles in a graph, where m is edges, n is vertices, and p is connected components. This formula provides a lower bound on the number of cycles.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing a graph's minimal cycle count, use the cyclomatic number formula to derive a lower bound based on edges, vertices, and connected components.

general_skills.title: Minimize Cycles via Connected Components
general_skills.principle: The minimal number of cycles occurs when the graph is connected (p=1), as this configuration minimizes the cyclomatic number and ensures each additional edge beyond a spanning tree contributes exactly one cycle.
general_skills.when_to_apply: To find the minimal cycle count, assume the graph is connected (p=1) and apply the cyclomatic number formula to compute the lower bound.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition in Iterative Elimination
general_skills.principle: When a process involves repeatedly removing every second element, the remaining elements are those divisible by increasing powers of the step size (e.g., 2, 4, 8, etc.).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simulating elimination steps that halve the remaining elements, identify the pattern of powers of the step size.

general_skills.title: Max Power of Base in Range
general_skills.principle: The final survivor in such a process is the highest power of the step size (e.g., 2) that is less than or equal to the original range.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the final result after iterative elimination, compute the maximum power of the base (e.g., 2) within the original domain.

general_skills.title: Structure-Based Final Result
general_skills.principle: Use the structure of the problem (e.g., divisibility by powers of two) to determine the final survivor by analyzing the elimination steps.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem reduces to a subset with a clear mathematical property (e.g., powers of a base), apply that property to find the final result.

general_skills.title: Arithmetic Sequence Sine Sum Simplification
general_skills.principle: Identify arithmetic sequences in trigonometric expressions and apply sum formulas to collapse them into compact forms using identities like the sum of sines in arithmetic progression.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering sums of sines with equally spaced angles, recognize the pattern and use the formula for the sum of such a sequence.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Identity Transformation
general_skills.principle: Leverage double-angle or product-to-sum identities to simplify products of sines and cosines, particularly when angles are related through symmetry or known relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with products of trigonometric functions involving angles that can be expressed in terms of simpler, related angles via identities.

general_skills.title: Decompose Composite Geometry
general_skills.principle: Break down complex shapes (e.g., cylinders with hemispheres) into simpler components to derive constraints and relationships between dimensions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing geometric configurations with multiple parts (e.g., containers, solids of revolution).

general_skills.title: Formulate Optimization via Calculus
general_skills.principle: Express volume or area as a function of variables, then use derivatives to find critical points and validate maxima under constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing quantities (e.g., volume, area) with continuous variables and boundary conditions.

general_skills.title: Validate via Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Evaluate critical points and endpoints to ensure solutions satisfy all geometric and physical constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving optimization problems with multiple valid ranges or boundary conditions.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Setup
general_skills.principle: Model geometric configurations with coordinates to translate angle and length relationships into algebraic equations for analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves complex geometric relationships requiring precise measurements or intersections.

general_skills.title: Vector Perpendicularity Check
general_skills.principle: Compute the dot product of vectors derived from key points to determine if lines are perpendicular, leveraging algebraic simplification.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying orthogonality between lines in a geometric figure through coordinate-based vector analysis.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Validation
general_skills.principle: Test special configurations (e.g., symmetric cases) to confirm general results, ensuring robustness across edge scenarios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When validating geometric conclusions through simplified or symmetric instances of the problem.

general_skills.title: Modular Congruence Translation
general_skills.principle: When a problem requires a number to end with k identical digits (e.g., 9s), translate it into a modular congruence condition (e.g., x ≡ -1 mod 10^k).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing the last k digits of a number or expressions involving factorials.

general_skills.title: Prime Exponent Analysis in Factorials
general_skills.principle: To determine divisibility by 10^k, compute the exponents of primes 2 and 5 in the product of factorials using Legendre's formula (sum of floor(n/p^i) for i ≥ 1).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying divisibility by powers of 10 in expressions involving factorials.

general_skills.title: Minimality Verification via Incremental Checks
general_skills.principle: To confirm a candidate value is minimal, systematically check consecutive values below it to ensure the condition is first satisfied at the candidate.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking the smallest n satisfying a combinatorial or number-theoretic condition.

general_skills.title: Translate Geometric Constraints into Algebraic Relations
general_skills.principle: Convert geometric conditions (e.g., perpendicular chords, cyclic polygons) into equations involving angles, lengths, or other measurable quantities to establish structural relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a problem involving geometric constraints that can be parameterized using angles or lengths.

general_skills.title: Optimize Trigonometric Expressions Under Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use trigonometric identities to express target quantities (e.g., area) in terms of variables derived from constraints, then maximize/minimize them using calculus or known maxima (e.g., sin(π/2) = 1).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing areas, angles, or other quantities in cyclic or geometric configurations with trigonometric dependencies.

general_skills.title: Decompose Complex Configurations into Simpler Components
general_skills.principle: Break down a polygon or geometric figure into simpler parts (e.g., triangles, central angles) to compute total area or other properties by summing contributions from individual components.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing cyclic polygons or figures with multiple constraints that can be separated into manageable sub-problems.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Place geometric entities in a coordinate system based on given constraints (e.g., tangency points, symmetry) to translate spatial relationships into algebraic expressions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves multiple circles and tangency conditions that can be represented via coordinates.

general_skills.title: Equation System Derivation
general_skills.principle: Formulate equations from geometric constraints (e.g., distances between centers, radii) and solve systems of equations to determine unknown quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems requiring simultaneous relationships between multiple geometric entities, such as tangent circles or inscribed shapes.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Constraint Handling
general_skills.principle: Use algebraic techniques (e.g., substitution, squaring both sides) to resolve absolute value or distance-based equations derived from geometric configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for variables in problems involving tangency, distance, or symmetry that produce equations with absolute values or square roots.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Absolute Values
general_skills.principle: Split absolute value inequalities into cases based on the sign of the expressions inside, then solve each case separately to find valid intervals.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering an inequality involving absolute values that require considering different sign scenarios.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification via Squaring
general_skills.principle: Square both sides of an inequality to eliminate absolute values, then solve the resulting quadratic or higher-degree equations to determine solution sets.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with absolute value inequalities where squaring both sides preserves the inequality's validity and simplifies the problem.

general_skills.title: Interval Combination and Validation
general_skills.principle: Combine intervals from different cases, eliminate invalid ranges, and verify that the final solution set satisfies the original inequality's constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After solving subcases of an inequality, to merge and refine the solution set into a consistent, final interval.

general_skills.title: Model Constraints as Equations
general_skills.principle: Translate real-world scenarios into mathematical equations by identifying relationships between variables and constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves counting or relationships between entities that can be expressed numerically.

general_skills.title: Factor to Find Integer Solutions
general_skills.principle: Decompose equations into factors to identify integer solutions that satisfy given constraints, especially when variables are bounded below by positive integers.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for integer values of variables in equations derived from combinatorial or geometric contexts.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Validity

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Total Calculation

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Equation Simplification
general_skills.principle: Simplify complex trigonometric equations involving multiple angles by leveraging identities and symmetry, especially when angles are constrained by geometric properties.

general_skills.title: Identify Necessary Conditions for Subset Partitioning
general_skills.principle: To determine if a set can be partitioned into two subsets with specific properties, first identify the minimal requirements for each subset (e.g., consecutive sequences, size constraints) and ensure the overall set meets these criteria.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing problems requiring partitioning into structured subsets (e.g., sequences, combinatorial configurations).

general_skills.title: Systematically Test Cases Based on Sequence Properties
general_skills.principle: Generate candidate solutions by leveraging known sequences (e.g., Fibonacci, triangular) and test their compatibility with the problem's constraints through case analysis and elimination.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When exploring number-theoretic or combinatorial problems involving specific number sequences or set partitions.

general_skills.title: Verify Disjointness and Coverage in Set Partitions
general_skills.principle: Ensure that proposed subsets satisfy both disjointness and complete coverage of the original set by cross-checking element inclusion and exclusion against the problem's definition.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When validating solutions for set-based problems requiring exact partitioning into defined categories.

general_skills.title: Modular Arithmetic and GCD Analysis
general_skills.principle: Translate problems into congruence conditions and use GCD to determine divisibility or solvability of equations, particularly when analyzing existence of multiples or solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When assessing whether a number has a multiple satisfying a specific modular condition (e.g., ending in a particular digit sequence).

general_skills.title: Case Analysis Based on Number Properties
general_skills.principle: Split problems into cases based on specific properties (e.g., primality, divisibility by small primes) to simplify and resolve distinct subproblems.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem's solution depends on distinct scenarios triggered by unique characteristics of numbers (e.g., primes 2 or 5 in this case).

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification via Differences
general_skills.principle: Compute differences between expressions to reduce complexity, leveraging identities like $a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)$ to simplify large terms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with sums of squares or similar expressions, compute differences to reveal underlying patterns or factorizations.

general_skills.title: Modular Divisibility Analysis
general_skills.principle: Use modular arithmetic to test divisibility by small primes, narrowing down GCD candidates by checking congruence modulo relevant primes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining common factors, analyze expressions modulo small primes to identify potential divisors efficiently.

general_skills.title: Euclidean Algorithm Reduction
general_skills.principle: Apply the Euclidean algorithm by reducing the problem to simpler forms (e.g., differences or moduli) to compute GCDs without full computation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When computing GCDs of large numbers, use differences, moduli, or other reductions to avoid direct calculation of large values.

general_skills.title: Enforce Spacing Constraints
general_skills.principle: To avoid palindromic substrings, ensure identical elements are spaced at least two positions apart to prevent adjacent or single-letter separations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When avoiding palindromic substrings in permutations of multiset elements.

general_skills.title: Permute Grouped Elements
general_skills.principle: Group identical elements and permute their positions in non-overlapping slots that satisfy spacing constraints to count valid arrangements.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When arranging multiset permutations with specific positional restrictions.

general_skills.title: Model with Arithmetic Sequences
general_skills.principle: Represent sequences with variables (e.g., a, a+d, a+2d) to encode problem constraints like order and spacing, then derive equations from given conditions (e.g., perimeter).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves ordered, evenly spaced elements or requires expressing relationships between variables.

general_skills.title: Apply Constraint-Based Filtering
general_skills.principle: Use problem-specific constraints (e.g., triangle inequality, integer conditions) to narrow down candidate solutions, ensuring they satisfy all derived equations and inequalities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying validity of potential solutions in combinatorial or geometric problems with multiple constraints.

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Enumeration
general_skills.principle: Iterate through feasible parameter ranges (e.g., integer values of d) to generate candidate solutions, then eliminate invalid cases based on derived constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting discrete solutions under structured conditions, such as integer side lengths or arithmetic progressions.

general_skills.title: Interval Partitioning via Function Bounds
general_skills.principle: Identify intervals where a function's value remains constant by solving inequalities derived from its definition, such as finding ranges of n where round(n^(1/4)) = m.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a function's output depends on a continuous transformation (e.g., roots, logs) and needs to be evaluated over discrete integers.

general_skills.title: Aggregation by Constant-Value Contributions
general_skills.principle: Compute the total sum by calculating the count of elements in each interval where the function is constant, then summing (count × 1/function_value) across all intervals.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When summing over a discrete domain with a function that is constant on subintervals, and the sum can be decomposed into contributions from each subinterval.

general_skills.title: Congruence Difference Principle
general_skills.principle: If two expressions a and b have the same remainder modulo m, then their difference (a - b) is divisible by m. This allows translating remainder conditions into divisibility requirements.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a problem involving congruence conditions on expressions, compute their difference to derive a divisibility constraint.

general_skills.title: Divisor Search with Constraints
general_skills.principle: To find the smallest valid value satisfying a divisor condition, systematically identify divisors of the target number that meet the constraint (e.g., size threshold), then select the smallest valid one.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When searching for the minimal value of an expression that must divide a given number while satisfying a lower bound or other constraints.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis by Input Properties
general_skills.principle: Split problems into cases based on key properties (e.g., sign, integer status) to isolate distinct scenarios for analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a function's behavior depends on multiple distinct cases that can be systematically categorized.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification with Floor Functions
