general_skills.principle: Use properties of floor functions (e.g., |floor(x)| = floor(|x|) for non-negative x) to reduce complex expressions to simpler forms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying expressions involving floor or absolute value functions through algebraic manipulation.

general_skills.title: Synthesis of Case Results
general_skills.principle: Combine outcomes from distinct cases to determine the complete range or solution set, ensuring no valid scenario is overlooked.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After analyzing all cases, consolidate results to identify the final set of possible values or conclusions.

general_skills.title: Geometric to Algebraic Translation
general_skills.principle: Convert geometric relationships (e.g., chord length, central angles) into algebraic equations to model probability distributions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing distances or angles in circular or symmetric configurations.

general_skills.title: Symmetry Simplification
general_skills.principle: Fix one entity (e.g., a point on a circle) to reduce complexity, leveraging symmetry to simplify probability calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: In problems involving uniform distributions on symmetric shapes or systems.

general_skills.title: Inverse Trig Inequality Solving
general_skills.principle: Solve equations involving inverse trigonometric functions (e.g., arcsin) and approximate roots to determine thresholds for probabilistic conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing continuous probability thresholds to discrete integer constraints.

general_skills.title: Modular Pattern Recognition
general_skills.principle: Identify repeating cycles in modular exponentiation sequences by computing initial terms and observing periodicity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying large exponents modulo a number, compute small exponents to detect cycles.

general_skills.title: Parity-Driven Cyclic Determination
general_skills.principle: Use the parity (even/odd) of exponents to determine the state in a cyclic pattern of modular results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a cycle alternates based on exponent parity, apply the parity of the target exponent to select the correct cycle position.

general_skills.title: Modular Simplification for Large Exponents
general_skills.principle: Reduce large exponents modulo a target number to avoid direct computation, leveraging modular arithmetic properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with impractical large exponents, compute the result modulo a relevant number (e.g., 1000 for last three digits).

general_skills.title: Greedy Construction under Adjacency Constraints
general_skills.principle: Start with the largest/smallest available digit, then iteratively select the next digit that is not consecutive to the previous one, ensuring all digits are used exactly once.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constructing numbers with constraints on adjacent digits, prioritize extremal digits first and enforce non-consecutive selection step-by-step.

general_skills.title: Systematic Digit Placement
general_skills.principle: At each step, choose the next digit that is not consecutive to the previous one, considering remaining digits and the need to use all digits exactly once.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When building numbers under adjacency constraints, ensure each choice adheres to the rule while maintaining completeness of the digit set.

general_skills.title: Day-of-Week Shift Calculation
general_skills.principle: Determine the day of the week for a date by calculating the number of days between two known dates, accounting for leap years and using modular arithmetic to adjust for weekly cycles.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given constraints about the day of the week for a date and needing to infer the day for a subsequent date across years.

general_skills.title: Constraint Synthesis
general_skills.principle: Combine multiple given conditions (e.g., days of the week for different years) to deduce the type of year (leap/common) and the starting day of a target date.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple facts about dates and days are provided, and the solution requires resolving contradictions or dependencies between them.

general_skills.title: Date Positioning via Week Cycles
general_skills.principle: Determine specific dates (e.g., the nth Sunday) in a month by counting weeks from the first day of the month and applying modular arithmetic.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When identifying a particular occurrence (e.g., a specific weekday) within a month based on the starting day of the month.

general_skills.title: Apply Arithmetic Sequence Formula
general_skills.principle: Use the formula $ a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d $ to find the term number corresponding to a specific value in an arithmetic sequence.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given a sequence with a common difference and a target value, solve for $ n $ to determine the position of the target.

general_skills.title: Adjust Term Count for Inclusive/Exclusive Conditions
general_skills.principle: If a problem asks for terms **before** a specific value, subtract 1 from the term number to exclude the target term itself.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the question requires counting terms up to but not including a specific value in a sequence.

general_skills.title: Angle Position Analysis
general_skills.principle: Determine central angles by analyzing angular positions relative to a diameter or reference line, using given angular measures and geometric constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When points are positioned relative to a diameter or known angle, calculate their central angles by subtracting or adding given angles to total circle measures.

general_skills.title: Sector Area Ratio Calculation
general_skills.principle: Compute the ratio of sector areas by applying the sector area formula (θ/360 × πr²) and simplifying the resulting fraction, leveraging the proportionality of central angles to area.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing sector areas to the whole circle, use central angles to derive the ratio and reduce fractions to lowest terms.

general_skills.title: Fraction Simplification
general_skills.principle: Simplify fractions by factoring numerators and denominators, ensuring the final ratio is expressed in its lowest terms (k/m) for problem-solving outputs.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After computing a fractional result, factor and divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor to achieve the simplest form.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric entities to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations, enabling precise distance and position calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When modeling 3D objects or complex spatial configurations to derive quantitative relationships.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Based Equation Solving
general_skills.principle: Set up equations based on geometric constraints (e.g., equal edge lengths) and solve them systematically to determine unknown parameters.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying regularity or symmetry in figures requires enforcing specific distance or proportionality conditions.

general_skills.title: Symmetry Simplification
general_skills.principle: Leverage inherent symmetry to reduce computational complexity and validate solutions by ensuring consistency across all symmetrically equivalent parts.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems with regular or symmetric structures, such as regular polyhedra or balanced geometric configurations.

general_skills.title: Coordinate System Setup
general_skills.principle: Model geometric problems using a coordinate system to translate spatial relationships into algebraic expressions for distance, area, and constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves geometric figures with precise spatial relationships requiring quantitative analysis.

general_skills.title: Region Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break complex regions into simpler sub-regions (e.g., strips, triangles) whose areas can be calculated individually and combined to solve the target problem.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a region's area requires analyzing overlapping or composite shapes through decomposition.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Area Calculation
general_skills.principle: Use coordinate geometry, area formulas, or integration to compute areas of shapes defined by constraints, including triangles and strips.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When precise area computation is needed for regions bounded by lines, curves, or geometric figures with known properties.

general_skills.title: Use Polynomial Identities for Reduction
general_skills.principle: Leverage given equations to replace higher-degree terms with lower-degree expressions, enabling systematic simplification of complex polynomials.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a polynomial equation defines a relationship between powers of a variable, use it to recursively reduce exponents.

general_skills.title: Apply Binomial Theorem for Coefficient Extraction
general_skills.principle: Expand expressions using the binomial theorem to compute coefficients, then adjust for polynomial constraints to isolate desired terms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires finding coefficients in a polynomial expansion, use binomial coefficients and simplify using given relations.

general_skills.title: Recognize Exponent Cycles for Simplification
general_skills.principle: Identify patterns or cycles in exponents to express high-degree terms as repeated applications of lower-degree relations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with high exponents that can be reduced through iterative substitution or modular arithmetic.

general_skills.title: Decompose expressions via binomial theorem
general_skills.principle: Use the binomial theorem to break down complex expressions into terms with structured exponents, identifying conditions for rationality through coefficient analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing expansions of binomials with irrational components to determine rational terms.

general_skills.title: Solve congruence systems for exponent conditions
general_skills.principle: Apply the Chinese Remainder Theorem to solve systems of congruences derived from divisibility requirements, ensuring exponents satisfy multiple modular constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining valid exponents that meet conflicting modular conditions in algebraic expansions.

general_skills.title: Count solutions in arithmetic progressions
general_skills.principle: Use arithmetic sequence formulas to count terms within a range that satisfy a linear congruence, leveraging first term, difference, and last term parameters.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When quantifying the number of integers in a range meeting specific modular equivalence conditions.

general_skills.title: Model Averages as Total/Count Relationships
general_skills.principle: Translate average value problems into equations by equating total value to average multiplied by count, then adjust for changes (e.g., adding a quarter).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given an average value and a scenario involving changes to total value or count.

general_skills.title: Systematic Variable Assignment for Coin Problems
general_skills.principle: Assign variables to each coin type and use their known values to form equations, ensuring all constraints (e.g., non-negative integers) are satisfied.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving multiple coin types with integer quantities and value constraints.

general_skills.title: Iterative Testing of Integer Solutions
general_skills.principle: Test feasible integer values for variables in derived equations to find combinations that satisfy all constraints simultaneously.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving systems with discrete, non-negative integer solutions that require trial-and-error validation.

general_skills.title: Model Multiplicative Sequences
general_skills.principle: Represent sequential percentage changes as algebraic expressions involving multiplicative factors, preserving the order of operations for accurate modeling.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with compounded percentage changes over multiple steps.

general_skills.title: Leverage Commutative Properties
general_skills.principle: Recognize that multiplication is commutative and associative, allowing rearrangement of operations without altering the final product.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing equivalent expressions involving multiplicative factors in different sequences.

general_skills.title: Verify Expression Equivalence
general_skills.principle: Simplify algebraic expressions to confirm equivalence through algebraic manipulation, ensuring consistency across different problem scenarios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When validating that rearranged operations yield the same result in complex multiplicative contexts.

general_skills.title: Substitute Variables for Constraint Simplification
general_skills.principle: Replace variables with expressions derived from constraints to reduce the problem to a single-variable function, enabling direct optimization techniques.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a constrained optimization problem, express all variables in terms of a single variable using the constraint.

general_skills.title: Apply Calculus to Find Critical Points
general_skills.principle: Use derivatives to identify critical points of a function, then evaluate the function at these points to determine maxima or minima under constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing a single-variable function derived from a constrained problem, compute derivatives to locate critical points.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification for Key Relationships
general_skills.principle: Factor or combine terms in complex expressions to reveal underlying patterns or relationships, such as simplifying to a product form for easier optimization.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with high-degree polynomials or symmetric expressions, simplify them to lower-degree forms or factored expressions to exploit constraints.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Break problems into distinct cases based on constraints or conditions to isolate valid solution paths.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves multiple scenarios or dependencies that require separate examination.

general_skills.title: Constraint Validation
general_skills.principle: Check solutions against problem constraints (e.g., non-zero denominators, inequality conditions) to eliminate extraneous or invalid results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving equations or inequalities with domain restrictions that must be explicitly satisfied.

general_skills.title: Distinctness Verification
general_skills.principle: Compare solutions from different cases to ensure they are unique and do not overlap under given constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple cases or methods yield potential solutions that could conflict or repeat.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric elements to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations, leveraging known segment lengths and slopes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves geometric configurations with known segment divisions or ratios, use coordinate placement to simplify calculations.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Ratio Translation
general_skills.principle: Convert trigonometric ratios (e.g., tangent of an angle) into algebraic expressions by relating them to side lengths in a coordinate or geometric setup.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given trigonometric values for angles in a triangle, express them as ratios of coordinates or segments to form equations.

general_skills.title: Quadratic Equation Resolution
general_skills.principle: Solve quadratic equations derived from geometric constraints, prioritizing physically meaningful solutions (e.g., positive lengths) to determine unknown quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When algebraic manipulations yield a quadratic equation, apply the quadratic formula and discard extraneous solutions based on problem context.

general_skills.title: Simplify via Symmetric Grouping
general_skills.principle: Identify structured patterns in polynomials by grouping terms to reduce complexity, such as pairing consecutive factors or substituting variables to form simpler expressions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a high-degree polynomial with symmetric or consecutive terms, group terms to create a lower-degree expression or substitution.

general_skills.title: Complete the Square for Minima
general_skills.principle: Transform quadratic expressions into squared terms plus a constant to directly determine their minimum or maximum values by setting the squared term to zero.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing expressions of the form $ a^2 + c $, use completion of the square to find extrema by solving $ a = 0 $.

general_skills.title: Apply Triangle Inequality Constraints
general_skills.principle: For a set of numbers, ensure that for any three elements a ≤ b ≤ c, a + b > c holds to guarantee non-degenerate triangles.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying that all subsets of size three in a sequence satisfy the triangle inequality.

general_skills.title: Systematic Constraint Validation
general_skills.principle: Iteratively add elements to a sequence while checking that each new element satisfies the inequality with all previous pairs to maintain validity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constructing a maximal set under strict inequality constraints.

general_skills.title: Sequence Structure Recognition
general_skills.principle: A strictly increasing sequence must satisfy each term being less than the sum of the two previous terms to ensure all triplets meet the triangle condition.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When designing sequences with global constraints on pairwise and triplet relationships.

general_skills.title: Recursive Pattern Simplification
general_skills.principle: Identify recursive definitions by analyzing base cases and stepwise transitions, then derive closed-form expressions by recognizing arithmetic progressions or cumulative increments.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with recursive functions that depend on conditional steps (e.g., base case or recursive calls).

general_skills.title: Case Analysis via Structural Properties
general_skills.principle: Split problems into cases based on inherent properties (e.g., parity, perfect squares) to isolate constraints and simplify recursive dependencies.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves conditional branching that depends on structural characteristics of the input (e.g., integer properties).

general_skills.title: Equation-Based Ratio Solving
general_skills.principle: Formulate algebraic relationships from derived expressions, then solve equations by equating ratios and leveraging number-theoretic constraints (e.g., integer solutions).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining specific values requires balancing recursive outputs through algebraic manipulation and ratio constraints.

general_skills.title: Chord-Length-Radius-Distance Relation
general_skills.principle: Use the formula for chord length $ 2\sqrt{r^2 - d^2} $ to relate a chord's length to the circle's radius and the distance from the center to the line.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given chord lengths and needing to connect them to geometric constraints involving a circle and parallel lines.

general_skills.title: Symmetry in Equal Chords
general_skills.principle: Equal chord lengths in symmetric configurations imply equidistance from the center, allowing deduction of proportional relationships between distances and lengths.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple chords of the same length are created by symmetrically placed lines or points in a geometric figure.

general_skills.title: Systematic Equation Setup
general_skills.principle: Derive algebraic equations from geometric constraints and solve them step-by-step to isolate unknown quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems that require translating geometric properties into algebraic relationships.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis Based on Structural Constraints
general_skills.principle: Divide the problem into distinct cases based on constraints, such as separating elements with conditions from those without, to simplify counting.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves multiple independent subproblems with differing constraints.

general_skills.title: Recurrence for Combinatorial Structures
general_skills.principle: Use recurrence relations to count structures like involutions, where each step builds on smaller instances of the same problem.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting configurations with recursive properties, such as permutations with specific cycle constraints.

general_skills.title: Independent Component Multiplication
general_skills.principle: Multiply counts of independent components when their choices are unrelated, such as free mappings and constrained mappings in separate domains.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem decomposes into independent subproblems with no overlapping constraints.

general_skills.title: Proportional Equations from Equal Contributions
general_skills.principle: When multiple entities contribute equal amounts based on proportional shares of their own quantities, assign a common variable to the equal contribution and express each entity's original amount in terms of that variable.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Use when a problem involves equal transfers based on fractional shares of distinct quantities.

general_skills.title: Conservation of Total Quantity in Transfers
general_skills.principle: In problems where money or other quantities are transferred between entities without external changes, the total quantity remains constant before and after the transfer.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Apply when verifying or calculating final distributions after transfers, ensuring total quantity is preserved.

general_skills.title: Fractional Part Calculation via Part-Whole Relationship
general_skills.principle: Determine the fraction of a total by comparing the final amount of a specific entity to the total quantity, simplifying expressions to find the ratio.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Use when computing the proportion of a quantity after transfers, leveraging algebraic simplification.

general_skills.title: Modular Decomposition via CRT
general_skills.principle: When solving congruences for composite moduli, decompose the modulus into coprime factors and solve separately using the Chinese Remainder Theorem.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target modulus factors into coprime components (e.g., 1000 = 8 × 125).

general_skills.title: Prime Exponent Counting
general_skills.principle: Count the exponents of primes (e.g., 5) in a product by summing floor divisions of the range by powers of the prime, adjusting for odd/even contributions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: To determine divisibility by prime powers in a product of sequential numbers or multiples.

general_skills.title: Structure-Based Modulus Simplification
general_skills.principle: Leverage the inherent properties of the product's components (e.g., parity, periodicity modulo small numbers) to simplify large modulus computations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the product's structure (e.g., all odd numbers) allows direct analysis of its residue class modulo a small integer.

general_skills.title: Prime Factorization via Legendre's Formula
general_skills.principle: To compute exponents of primes in n!, use Legendre's formula: sum floor(n/p^k) for k ≥ 1. This method systematically determines prime factors in factorials.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When decomposing factorials into prime factors for number theory or combinatorics problems.

general_skills.title: Adjust Exponents for Perfect Squares
general_skills.principle: For the largest perfect square divisor, take the largest even exponent ≤ each prime's exponent in the factorization. This ensures the product is a perfect square.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When identifying square divisors of numbers or factorials in algebraic or number theory contexts.

general_skills.title: Square Root of Prime Factorization
general_skills.principle: Taking the square root of a prime factorization halves all exponents. Sum these halved exponents to find the required total in olympiad-style problems.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing square roots of products or solving problems involving exponents and prime factors in algebra or number theory.

general_skills.title: Prime Factorization and Even Exponents
general_skills.principle: Decompose numbers into prime factors and ensure that the sum of exponents for each prime in a group is even to form a perfect square.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing problems requiring groupings where products must satisfy parity conditions on prime exponents.

general_skills.title: Vector Space Over GF(2) Grouping
general_skills.principle: Model numbers as binary vectors over GF(2) based on prime exponents, then find linearly dependent subsets that sum to zero to form valid groups.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving combinatorial groupings with constraints on multiplicative properties or parity conditions.

general_skills.title: Leverage Mathematical Structures
general_skills.principle: Identify known mathematical properties (e.g., Pythagorean triples) to narrow down candidate solutions under problem constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves constraints that align with established mathematical relationships.

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Exploration
general_skills.principle: Enumerate all possible cases within given constraints (e.g., digit ranges) to find valid solutions systematically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires checking a finite set of possibilities under specific bounds.

general_skills.title: Prime Factor Analysis
general_skills.principle: Factor candidate numbers to extract prime factors and determine the maximum among them.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the goal is to identify the largest prime factor of a number derived from constraints.

general_skills.title: Model Time-Based Relationships
general_skills.principle: Introduce variables for current and past/future time points to represent age differences, ensuring equations capture the temporal dynamics described in the problem.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering problems involving age differences or time-based conditions that require tracking past/future states.

general_skills.title: Translate Verbal Conditions to Equations
general_skills.principle: Break down complex statements into algebraic relationships by identifying key numerical relationships (e.g., 'twice as old', 'seven years from...') and converting them into equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with word problems that require interpreting abstract or nested temporal conditions into mathematical expressions.

general_skills.title: Solve Systems via Substitution
general_skills.principle: Use substitution to express variables in terms of others, leveraging derived relationships to simplify and solve systems of equations systematically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving systems of equations where one variable can be expressed directly in terms of another, enabling stepwise resolution of unknowns.

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Counting for Valid Pairs
general_skills.principle: Calculate the number of valid pairs by summing over structured differences (e.g., label differences ≥50) using arithmetic series or combinatorial formulas.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the count of pairs satisfying a specific numerical condition in a permutation or combinatorial setup.

general_skills.title: Linearity of Expectation for Expected Value
general_skills.principle: Compute the expected value by summing individual probabilities across all relevant events, even when events are not independent.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating the expected number of occurrences of a property across a large set of structured elements (e.g., edges in a graph).

general_skills.title: Probability via Uniform Permutations
general_skills.principle: Determine the probability of a pair satisfying a condition by dividing the count of valid permutations by the total number of permutations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing random assignments (permutations) and calculating the likelihood of specific label or value relationships.

general_skills.title: Factor Polynomials Using Identities
general_skills.principle: Decompose complex expressions into simpler factors using known algebraic identities (e.g., sum/difference of cubes) to reveal underlying patterns.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering polynomials that can be expressed as standard forms (e.g., a³ ± b³) to simplify or analyze their structure.

general_skills.title: Identify Telescoping Products
general_skills.principle: Recognize cancellation patterns in products by factoring terms such that consecutive terms in the sequence cancel, reducing the product to a manageable form.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing products where terms can be rearranged or factored to create overlapping cancellations between consecutive elements.

general_skills.title: Simplify Infinite Products via Limits
general_skills.principle: Evaluate infinite products by computing the limit of partial products after telescoping, focusing on dominant terms as the number of factors approaches infinity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After identifying telescoping behavior, analyze the limiting behavior of the remaining terms to determine the product's value.

general_skills.title: Segment-based Cumulative Summation
general_skills.principle: Break the problem into segments (e.g., numbers by digit length) and compute cumulative totals for each segment to identify the range containing the target.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves counting elements in a sequence with varying contributions per segment.

general_skills.title: Range Isolation via Subtraction
general_skills.principle: Subtract cumulative totals to determine the exact segment and position within that segment where the target lies.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target is within a larger cumulative range, and you need to isolate the specific segment and offset.

general_skills.title: Digit Position Analysis
general_skills.principle: Analyze the structure of the segment (e.g., number of digits per element) to pinpoint the exact digit within the identified range.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target lies within a segment with uniform or predictable element properties (e.g., fixed digit length).

general_skills.title: Vieta's Formulas with Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use Vieta's formulas to relate coefficients of a polynomial to symmetric sums of its roots, especially when roots are constrained to be positive real numbers.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given a polynomial with specified root properties (e.g., all roots positive) and coefficients to relate to root sums/products.

general_skills.title: Inequality-Based Extremum Search
general_skills.principle: Apply inequalities (e.g., Cauchy-Schwarz) to find minima/maxima of expressions involving root sums or products, leveraging equality conditions for optimal solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing coefficients or root configurations under symmetric constraints, such as minimizing/maximizing a sum under fixed product or sum constraints.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis by Parameter
general_skills.principle: Break problems into distinct cases based on a key parameter (e.g., arithmetic sequence differences) to systematically explore all possibilities while ensuring completeness.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem's solution depends on multiple distinct scenarios that can be parameterized and analyzed separately.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Permutation Counting
general_skills.principle: Adjust permutation counts by applying constraints (e.g., non-zero leading digits) to filter valid arrangements, ensuring only permissible configurations are counted.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating permutations of a set under specific restrictions that invalidate certain arrangements.

general_skills.title: Decompose Complex Shapes into Simpler Components
general_skills.principle: Break down a complex figure into known shapes (e.g., trapezoids, triangles) to compute total area by summing individual components.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a figure is divided into regions with defined properties, use decomposition to isolate and calculate each part's area.

general_skills.title: Apply Coordinate Geometry for Area Calculations
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to vertices and use geometric formulas (e.g., trapezoid area) to compute areas based on coordinate positions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves precise geometric configurations, use coordinate systems to determine lengths, heights, and areas.

general_skills.title: Simplify Ratios Using Standard Area Formulas
general_skills.principle: Compute ratios of areas by applying standard formulas (e.g., regular hexagon area, trapezoid area) and reduce fractions to lowest terms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing regions of a figure, use standardized area expressions and simplify resulting fractions to find proportions.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis by Structural Properties
general_skills.principle: Break down complex problems into distinct cases based on inherent structural characteristics (e.g., prime powers or products of distinct primes) to simplify analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves numbers with specific properties that can be categorized into distinct structural forms.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Factorization for Sum Conditions
general_skills.principle: Use algebraic identities to transform and simplify conditions, such as expressing sums of divisors as products (e.g., (1+p)(1+q)), to identify valid representations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying if a number can be expressed in a specific form through algebraic manipulation of its structural properties.

general_skills.title: Systematic Candidate Verification
general_skills.principle: Iterate through each candidate in the target range and apply derived conditions to eliminate invalid cases based on constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating a finite set of numbers against specific mathematical criteria requiring exhaustive checking.

general_skills.title: Coverage Equations and GCD Constraints
general_skills.principle: Model coverage requirements as equations (e.g., sum of reciprocals equals 1) and enforce pairwise disjointness via gcd conditions to ensure sequences partition the domain.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires partitioning a domain into non-overlapping sequences with specific periodicity constraints.

general_skills.title: Systematic Constraint Exploration
general_skills.principle: Systematically test integer solutions by combining algebraic equations with gcd-based constraints to identify valid configurations that satisfy all problem conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems with multiple interdependent constraints that require exhaustive or structured search over discrete variables.

general_skills.title: Polynomial Difference Divisibility
general_skills.principle: For polynomials with integer coefficients, the difference P(m) - P(n) is divisible by m - n. Use this to derive constraints on M for divisibility conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing polynomial constraints involving integer coefficients and differences between points.

general_skills.title: LCM-Based Divisibility Enforcement
general_skills.principle: To satisfy divisibility for arbitrary integers, M must be a multiple of the least common multiple of the required moduli derived from the problem's constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When ensuring that a value M satisfies modular conditions for all possible integer inputs.

general_skills.title: Modular Constraints for Arbitrary Inputs
general_skills.principle: For arbitrary integers, enforce congruence conditions by ensuring M is a multiple of the necessary moduli to satisfy all possible differences.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying that a value M meets divisibility requirements for all integer combinations in a problem.

general_skills.title: Balance Products via Geometric Mean
general_skills.principle: Estimate the target value for optimization by computing the geometric mean of the total product, then refine through systematic grouping.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing the maximum of multiple products under constraints on element distribution.

general_skills.title: Systematic Grouping Analysis
general_skills.principle: Test partitions by distributing high/low values strategically to balance products, eliminating invalid configurations that violate constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When partitioning a set into subsets to minimize the maximum subset product or similar optimization tasks.

general_skills.title: Maximize Equality Among Products
general_skills.principle: Prioritize groupings where products are as close as possible to the geometric mean, ensuring no single product dominates excessively.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking minimal maximum values in multi-subset product problems with distinct element constraints.

general_skills.title: Variable Substitution Based on Given Relationships
general_skills.principle: Express one variable in terms of another using direct constraints (e.g., differences) to reduce problem complexity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem provides a fixed relationship between variables (e.g., x - y = 60), substitute to simplify expressions.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Manipulation to Eliminate Radicals
general_skills.principle: Square both sides of equations involving radicals to derive constraints, ensuring consistency with problem conditions (e.g., non-perfect square k).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with sums or differences of square roots that must equal another square root expression.

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Analysis for Validity
general_skills.principle: Generate candidate solutions, test them against all problem constraints, and eliminate invalid cases (e.g., non-integer, non-positive values).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple solutions exist and explicit conditions (e.g., non-perfect square, positivity) must be verified.

general_skills.title: Expand and Simplify with Identities
general_skills.principle: Expand algebraic expressions systematically, then simplify by combining like terms and applying known identities (e.g., polynomial roots, symmetry properties).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a product or expression involving roots of unity or symmetric polynomials.

general_skills.title: Leverage Root Properties for Substitution
general_skills.principle: Use fundamental identities derived from root properties (e.g., $1 + w + w^2 = 0$, $w^3 = 1$) to substitute known values and reduce complex expressions to simpler forms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying expressions involving roots of equations or symmetric algebraic structures.

general_skills.title: Optimize Ratio via Parameter Balance
general_skills.principle: To minimize a ratio of a quantity to a sum, prioritize maximizing the denominator (sum) while minimizing the numerator (value) through strategic parameter variation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking to minimize a ratio involving a numeric value and a derived sum (e.g., digits, terms), adjust parameters to balance the two components.

general_skills.title: Systematic Candidate Exploration
general_skills.principle: Iterate over key parameters (e.g., digit sums) to identify candidates, then select the minimal value for each parameter to ensure optimal results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating discrete domains (e.g., digit sums, combinatorial configurations), systematically test candidates by varying critical parameters and selecting the best fit.

general_skills.title: Decompose divisor count into multiplicative factors
general_skills.principle: Factor the target number of divisors into products of (2a_i + 1) terms based on prime exponents in N², considering constraints like N being a multiple of 83.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the prime exponents of N from the divisor count of N².

general_skills.title: Case analysis for minimal N
general_skills.principle: Evaluate different factorizations of the divisor count, prioritizing cases that assign higher exponents to smaller primes to minimize N.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple prime exponent configurations are possible and the goal is to find the smallest N.

general_skills.title: Optimize prime exponent assignments
general_skills.principle: Assign higher exponents to smaller primes in the factorization to minimize the overall value of N, ensuring N is a multiple of required primes like 83.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When balancing prime exponents to satisfy divisor constraints while minimizing N.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis by Coin Type
general_skills.principle: Break down the problem into distinct cases based on the number of each coin type selected, then eliminate cases that do not satisfy the target value constraint.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining valid combinations for a target sum with multiple coin types, partition possibilities by coin counts and filter out invalid scenarios.

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Counting for Probability
general_skills.principle: Calculate total possible outcomes using combinations (e.g., C(n, k)) and favorable outcomes by multiplying counts of valid selections for each coin type.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When computing probabilities involving discrete selections from multiple categories, use combinatorial formulas to determine favorable and total outcome counts.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Based Case Splitting
general_skills.principle: When a problem requires inclusion of specific elements and additional constraints, split the problem into cases based on the constraints (e.g., whether a required element is included or excluded) and compute valid combinations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with multiple constraints that require certain elements to be included or excluded.

general_skills.title: Complementary Counting
general_skills.principle: Calculate the total number of combinations under constraints and subtract invalid cases that violate the constraints to determine the valid count.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves constraints that can be efficiently addressed by subtracting invalid scenarios from the total.

general_skills.title: Factor Polynomials for Simplification
general_skills.principle: Decompose complex polynomials into simpler factors to isolate conditions for real roots.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a high-degree polynomial, attempt factoring to break it into manageable components.

general_skills.title: Use Discriminants for Real Root Conditions
general_skills.principle: For quadratic factors, compute discriminants to determine parameter ranges ensuring real roots.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing polynomials with potential real roots, apply discriminant conditions to quadratic components.

general_skills.title: Compute Interval Measures for Probability
general_skills.principle: Calculate the length of valid parameter intervals and divide by total range to determine probabilities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for parameter ranges that satisfy conditions, compute interval lengths and normalize for probability.

general_skills.title: Use Tangent Addition for Arctangent Sums
general_skills.principle: When given an identity involving sums of arctangent terms, apply the tangent addition formula to convert the sum into a single tangent expression, leveraging the identity tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B)/(1 - tan A tan B).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with equations that equate sums of arctangent functions to a constant angle, such as π/2, and the identity must hold for all variable inputs.

general_skills.title: Equate Coefficients for Universal Identities
general_skills.principle: If an equation involving variables holds for all values of the variable, equate coefficients of corresponding terms across both sides of the equation to derive constraints on unknowns.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for parameters in identities that must hold for all positive real numbers or other universal domains.

general_skills.title: Simplify via Algebraic Identities
general_skills.principle: Simplify complex expressions by expanding products, combining like terms, and applying algebraic identities (e.g., (a + b)^2 - 2ab) to compute target quantities efficiently.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When reducing expressions involving squared terms or products of variables after deriving linear relationships between them.

general_skills.title: Parity-Based Categorization
general_skills.principle: Categorize elements by parity (even/odd) to determine valid combinations that satisfy sum constraints, leveraging combinatorial counts for each category.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires counting combinations with sum parity constraints, split the set into even and odd subsets and compute valid combinations.

general_skills.title: Total Minus Invalid Cases
general_skills.principle: Calculate total valid cases by first computing all possibilities that meet the primary condition, then subtract cases that violate secondary constraints (e.g., sum thresholds).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires filtering a large set of candidates by multiple criteria, compute the total valid set and subtract exceptions explicitly enumerated.

general_skills.title: Apply Standard Summation Formulas
general_skills.principle: Use known formulas for sums of integers and cubes to simplify complex expressions and derive relationships between variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering summation expressions that can be reduced using established mathematical identities.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Equation Transformation
general_skills.principle: Transform equations through substitution and simplification to isolate variables and reveal underlying structural relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with complex equations requiring manipulation to extract solvable forms or constraints.

general_skills.title: Constraint Verification
general_skills.principle: Check derived solutions against problem-specific constraints (e.g., modular conditions, inequalities) to ensure validity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After solving equations, when verifying that solutions satisfy all problem requirements and edge cases.

general_skills.title: Modular Pattern Recognition
general_skills.principle: Identify periodic structures in sequences by partitioning terms based on congruence classes (e.g., modulo 4) to simplify summation or series analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a series exhibits periodic coefficients or terms that repeat with a fixed interval.

general_skills.title: Special Function Representation
general_skills.principle: Express complex series as combinations of known special functions (e.g., zeta function) to leverage their analytic properties and asymptotic expansions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a series can be reformulated in terms of functions like the Riemann zeta function or its derivatives for evaluation.

general_skills.title: Asymptotic Divergence Cancellation
general_skills.principle: Analyze divergent terms in series expansions by expanding around critical points (e.g., s=1) and canceling infinities through algebraic manipulation or derivative-based techniques.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating limits involving divergent components, such as zeta function behavior near poles, by combining expansions with cancellation of leading-order terms.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Side Length Inference
general_skills.principle: In right triangles, use sine, cosine, or tangent of given angles to compute side lengths relative to known hypotenuse or legs.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When trigonometric ratios and right-angle constraints are provided in a geometric configuration.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Distance Calculation
general_skills.principle: Compute distances between points using their coordinates via the distance formula, leveraging axis-aligned or derived coordinate systems.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When points are defined or can be parameterized in a coordinate plane with explicit or inferable coordinates.

general_skills.title: Constraint Consistency Verification
general_skills.principle: Validate solutions by ensuring they satisfy all given geometric, trigonometric, and algebraic constraints simultaneously.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After deriving a solution, when multiple conditions (e.g., angles, lengths, coordinates) must align for correctness.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis by Structural Constraints
general_skills.principle: Break problems into distinct scenarios based on key properties (e.g., which digit is repeated, where it appears) to isolate valid configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves multiple mutually exclusive subcases defined by specific structural conditions (e.g., positions, values, or counts).

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Counting with Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use permutations and combinations to count valid arrangements while enforcing distinctness and exclusion of invalid patterns (e.g., avoiding duplicates or overlapping cases).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting configurations that require selecting positions, values, and ensuring adherence to specific constraints (e.g., unique digits, fixed elements).

general_skills.title: Mutual Exclusivity Verification
general_skills.principle: Ensure all cases are non-overlapping and cover all possibilities to prevent overcounting or undercounting by systematically eliminating invalid configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When combining multiple cases to verify completeness and avoid double-counting or missing scenarios.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition in Recursive Sequences
general_skills.principle: Identify structural invariants or simplifications in recursive definitions to uncover hidden relationships between terms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When sequences are defined recursively and require analyzing their long-term behavior or properties.

general_skills.title: Geometric-to-Algebraic Translation
general_skills.principle: Convert geometric conditions (e.g., right triangles) into algebraic equations, then simplify to derive constraints on variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When problems involve geometric interpretations that can be reformulated using algebraic identities or number-theoretic properties.

general_skills.title: Range Analysis for Perfect Squares
general_skills.principle: Solve inequalities involving perfect squares to determine valid integer solutions within a specified range.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting solutions requiring a quantity (e.g., n) to satisfy both algebraic and numerical constraints.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Setup
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric figures based on given constraints, leveraging known properties (e.g., right triangles, circumcircles) to simplify calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves geometric configurations that can be modeled with coordinates, such as triangles, circles, or tangents.

general_skills.title: Circle and Tangent Properties
general_skills.principle: Use the fact that tangents to a circle are perpendicular to radii and that the hypotenuse of a right triangle is the diameter of its circumcircle to determine key points and relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with circumcircles, tangents, or right triangles, to find centers, intersection points, or perpendicularity conditions.

general_skills.title: Parallel Line Proportions
general_skills.principle: Establish vector or coordinate relationships between parallel lines to derive proportional constraints, enabling the solution of unknown points or lengths.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When parallelism is given or implied, to set up equations that relate coordinates or vectors of lines and points.

general_skills.title: Model as Permutations with Constraints
general_skills.principle: Recognize that problems involving unique assignments (e.g., placing non-attacking rooks) can be modeled as permutations with specific constraints on positions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires assigning distinct elements to positions with restrictions on certain elements.

general_skills.title: Adjust Choices for Constrained Positions
general_skills.principle: For constrained positions, reduce available options based on forbidden values or conditions, then compute permutations for remaining elements.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When specific elements (e.g., rows, columns) have restricted choices that must be accounted for in the total count.

general_skills.title: Decompose and Multiply Valid Configurations
general_skills.principle: Break the problem into independent parts (e.g., constrained and unconstrained sections), compute valid configurations for each, and multiply their counts.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem can be split into distinct subproblems with independent solutions that can be combined multiplicatively.

general_skills.title: Factor by Rearranging and Adding Constants
general_skills.principle: Transform equations into a product form by rearranging terms and adding constants to enable factoring, especially when the equation involves two variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a diophantine equation that can be rearranged into a product of binomials equal to a constant.

general_skills.title: Enumerate Integer Factor Pairs of a Constant
general_skills.principle: For a product of two integers equal to a constant, systematically list all integer factor pairs (positive and negative) to find all possible solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving equations where the product of two expressions equals a constant, particularly when the constant is prime or has limited divisors.

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Probability Modeling
general_skills.principle: Use combinatorial selection (n choose k) to count favorable outcomes in independent events, multiplying by individual probabilities for exact success counts.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating probabilities for exactly k successes in n independent trials with known success/failure probabilities.

general_skills.title: Binomial Probability Formula
general_skills.principle: Apply the binomial formula P(k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k) to compute exact probabilities for independent events with two outcomes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When modeling scenarios with independent trials, binary outcomes, and fixed numbers of trials.

general_skills.title: Fraction Simplification
general_skills.principle: Simplify fractions by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor to ensure reduced form.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After computing probabilities or combinatorial results, to express answers in lowest terms.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis via Constraints
general_skills.principle: When faced with divisibility conditions, split possibilities into cases based on structural constraints (e.g., n must be a power of 3 if n divides 3^n).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires narrowing down candidates through logical constraints.

general_skills.title: Modular Arithmetic for Divisibility
general_skills.principle: Use modular arithmetic to simplify large exponent checks, such as verifying $ a^k \equiv b \mod m $ to confirm divisibility conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying divisibility of large expressions like $ 3^n - 1 $ by smaller numbers like $ n - 1 $.

general_skills.title: Prime Power Divisor Insight
general_skills.principle: If a number divides a prime power (e.g., $ 3^n $), it must itself be a power of that prime, leveraging prime factorization properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing divisors of expressions like $ p^k $ where $ p $ is prime.

general_skills.title: Decompose numerical patterns into place-value expressions
general_skills.principle: Break down numbers into their digit-based components to form algebraic equations representing their structure.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves digit-based numbers or positional values (e.g., hundreds, tens, ones).

general_skills.title: Factor common terms to simplify equations
general_skills.principle: Identify and extract common factors from equations to reduce complexity and isolate target variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying linear equations or expressions with repeated coefficients.

general_skills.title: Solve linear equations via arithmetic isolation
general_skills.principle: Isolate variables through inverse operations (e.g., division, subtraction) and verify solutions by substitution.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for unknowns in single-variable linear equations derived from problem constraints.

general_skills.title: Logarithmic Variable Isolation
general_skills.principle: When a variable appears in an exponent, take logarithms of both sides to isolate it, leveraging the power rule (log(a^b) = b log a) to express the variable as a ratio of logarithms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for a variable in an exponential equation where the variable is in the exponent.

general_skills.title: Logarithmic Identity Simplification
general_skills.principle: Use the identity log_b(a) * log_a(c) = log_b(c) to simplify chains of logarithmic terms, reducing complex products to simpler expressions or constants.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying products of logarithms with nested bases or when recognizing patterns that collapse through logarithmic identities.

general_skills.title: Derive Geometric Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use properties of geometric figures (e.g., equiangular hexagons having parallel opposite sides) to establish algebraic relationships between side lengths and angles.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing a figure's structure to find constraints on its dimensions or configurations.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Boundary Conditions
general_skills.principle: Evaluate critical values (e.g., tangency points) to eliminate invalid configurations and identify thresholds for valid ranges of variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining boundaries for parameters that affect geometric feasibility or intersection conditions.

general_skills.title: Synthesize Constraints for Valid Ranges
general_skills.principle: Combine multiple geometric and algebraic constraints to narrow down valid intervals for variables, ensuring all conditions (e.g., circle intersections) are satisfied.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When resolving problems requiring simultaneous fulfillment of multiple interdependent constraints.

general_skills.title: Fixed Order Subset Selection
general_skills.principle: When a sequence must be in a specific order (e.g., decreasing or increasing), the number of valid permutations is determined by the number of ways to choose the elements for that sequence, as their order is fixed once selected.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a sequence's order is constrained to be strictly increasing or decreasing, and the rest of the permutation is determined by subset selection.

general_skills.title: Overlap Constraint Enforcement
general_skills.principle: When two sequences are connected at a point with an order constraint (e.g., a6 < a7), the critical condition is that the minimum of the first sequence is less than the minimum of the second sequence, ensuring compatibility between the two parts.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When two ordered segments share a boundary with a strict inequality constraint, enforce that the minimum of the first segment is less than the minimum of the second.

general_skills.title: Decomposition into Independent Parts
general_skills.principle: When a problem can be decomposed into independent parts with fixed order constraints, the total number of permutations is the product of the number of ways to choose elements for each part, considering their dependencies.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a permutation is split into non-overlapping segments with fixed order constraints, compute the product of subset choices for each segment.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Identity Expansion
general_skills.principle: Use multiple-angle identities to express complex trigonometric expressions in terms of simpler components, enabling algebraic simplification.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with equations involving higher multiples of angles (e.g., sin(5θ)) that can be expanded using known identities.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Equation Solving
general_skills.principle: Solve trigonometric equations by isolating variables and verifying solutions against domain constraints (e.g., acute angles) to ensure validity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving equations with trigonometric functions that require checking for valid solutions within specified ranges.

general_skills.title: Double-Angle Formula Application
general_skills.principle: Apply double-angle identities to compute tangent values from known sine and cosine values, leveraging algebraic relationships between trigonometric functions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When deriving tangent values from known sine/cosine values or when simplifying expressions involving double angles.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Assignment for Geometric Configurations
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to points in a geometric figure to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations, enabling precise calculations and constraint satisfaction.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves complex geometric configurations with relative positions or lengths that can be modeled via coordinate systems.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification to Identify Invariants
general_skills.principle: Derive algebraic expressions from geometric constraints and simplify them to uncover invariant quantities (e.g., fixed values) that remain unchanged under varying parameters.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking minimal or maximal values in problems where variables are constrained but not uniquely determined.

general_skills.title: Systematic Area Calculation via Coordinates
general_skills.principle: Use coordinate geometry formulas (e.g., shoelace formula) to compute areas of polygons defined by points in a coordinate plane, ensuring accuracy through systematic substitution and simplification.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating areas of triangles or polygons in problems involving coordinate-based geometric setups.

general_skills.title: Start with smallest primes in factorization
general_skills.principle: Begin prime factorization by testing divisibility by the smallest primes first, leveraging patterns like ending digits for 2/5 or alternating sums for 11.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When decomposing a composite number into primes, prioritize testing divisibility by small primes in ascending order.

general_skills.title: Iterative division to reduce composite numbers
general_skills.principle: Repeatedly divide the number by identified prime factors until all remaining factors are prime, systematically reducing the problem size at each step.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When breaking down a composite number, iteratively divide by primes until no further factorization is possible.

general_skills.title: Sum prime factors after complete factorization
general_skills.principle: Once all prime factors are identified, sum them directly to compute the required result, ensuring no composite factors remain.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After fully factorizing a number into primes, add the prime components to derive the target quantity.

general_skills.title: Count Valid Configurations Under Constraints
general_skills.principle: Identify all configurations satisfying a specific condition (e.g., O's forming a line) by enumerating possibilities and applying combinatorial rules.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires counting valid board states under a particular rule or constraint.

general_skills.title: Subtract Overlapping Cases
general_skills.principle: Adjust total counts by subtracting configurations where multiple conditions are simultaneously met (e.g., both O's and X's form lines) to ensure accuracy.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves exclusion of invalid overlaps between competing conditions.

general_skills.title: Count Disjoint Line Pairs
general_skills.principle: Systematically count pairs of disjoint lines (rows/columns) to identify overlapping configurations that require adjustment in combinatorial calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing interactions between multiple winning conditions in grid-based problems.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis by Sign Combinations
general_skills.principle: Split possible scenarios based on the signs of variables to identify which combinations yield maximum or minimum values.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing products or sums of functions with bounded ranges, consider cases where variables are positive, negative, or mixed.

general_skills.title: Evaluate Extreme Value Products
general_skills.principle: Test the product of extreme values (e.g., most negative or most positive) within given ranges to identify potential maximum or minimum outcomes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the range of a composite function, compute products of boundary values from the input ranges.

general_skills.title: Verify Attainability of Extremes
general_skills.principle: Confirm that the candidate maximum/minimum value is achievable by ensuring the required input values lie within the given ranges.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After identifying a candidate extremum, validate that the corresponding inputs are within the defined domain of the functions.

general_skills.title: Symmetry in Probability Comparisons
general_skills.principle: When comparing two independent events with identical distributions, the probability of one being greater than the other equals half the difference between 1 and the probability of equality.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Use this when dealing with symmetric probability distributions where the goal is to find the likelihood of one variable exceeding another.

general_skills.title: Fraction Simplification via Common Denominators
general_skills.principle: Convert all fractions to a common denominator to add or compare them, then simplify the result to its lowest terms by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Apply this when combining probabilities or comparing fractions in algebraic or combinatorial contexts.

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Enumeration for Equality Probabilities
general_skills.principle: Calculate the probability of equality by considering all pairs of outcomes where the values match, multiplying their individual probabilities and summing the results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Use this to determine equality probabilities in scenarios involving discrete, independent events with finite outcome sets.

general_skills.title: Decompose Complex Expressions
general_skills.principle: Break down multi-term expressions into simpler components using algebraic identities to isolate manageable parts for summation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a complex expression involving multiple variables and operations, factor or split it into separable terms.

general_skills.title: Leverage Symmetry in Summation
general_skills.principle: Recognize symmetric patterns in multi-variable sums to simplify computations by exploiting equal contributions from symmetric variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When summing over symmetric domains (e.g., variables with identical ranges), use symmetry to reduce computational complexity.

general_skills.title: Apply Linearity of Summation
general_skills.principle: Use the linearity of summation to separate and compute individual terms independently, then combine results for the total.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating sums with additive components, compute each term's contribution separately and aggregate the results.

general_skills.title: Parameterize Known Structures
general_skills.principle: Use standard parameterizations (e.g., Pythagorean triples) to generate candidate solutions that satisfy structural constraints like coprimality or divisibility.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves integer solutions to geometric or number-theoretic constraints with known parametric forms.

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Testing
general_skills.principle: Test small, minimal cases to identify the smallest solution that meets all constraints, ensuring no smaller valid configurations are overlooked.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking minimal solutions in combinatorial or olympiad-style problems with discrete constraints.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Condition Verification
general_skills.principle: Translate geometric or number-theoretic conditions (e.g., ratios, coprimality) into algebraic expressions to verify properties like perfect squares or divisibility.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When validating properties of candidate solutions through direct algebraic computation.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Identity Simplification
general_skills.principle: Use trigonometric identities to rewrite complex equations into simpler forms, enabling analysis of solution behavior.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying equations involving multiple trigonometric terms or requiring transformation into a manageable function.

general_skills.title: Function Behavior Analysis
general_skills.principle: Analyze the number of solutions in a given interval by transforming the equation into a function and determining parameter ranges that yield multiple solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the conditions under which an equation has a specified number of solutions in a domain, particularly involving parameter-dependent functions.

general_skills.title: Edge Case Exclusion
general_skills.principle: Identify and exclude special cases (e.g., overlapping roots or fixed solutions) that could distort the count of valid solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving equations with constraints that require careful handling of specific points or overlaps in solution sets.

general_skills.title: Multiplicative Principle for Independent Choices
general_skills.principle: When choices are independent across steps, the total number of combinations is the product of the number of options available at each step.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Use this when a problem involves sequential decisions where each step's outcome does not affect the others.

general_skills.title: Count Options in Sequential Steps
general_skills.principle: Break down the problem into individual steps, identify the number of valid options for each, and compute their product to find the total combinations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Apply this when a problem requires aggregating choices across distinct, sequential phases with clear constraints.

general_skills.title: Recognize Independent Constraints
general_skills.principle: Distinguish between steps where constraints are isolated to specific phases, ensuring each step's options are calculated independently.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Use this when a problem involves multiple stages with separate limitations that do not cross-pollinate between stages.

general_skills.title: Reverse Position Adjustment
general_skills.principle: When tracking positions through sequential deletions, adjust the target position by adding the number of removed elements before it in each step, working backward through operations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving multiple layers of deletions or transformations that alter sequence structure.

general_skills.title: Cyclic Pattern Mapping
general_skills.principle: For sequences with repeating patterns, compute the original element by taking the position modulo the cycle length, adjusting for zero-based or one-based indexing as needed.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the original sequence is periodic or cyclic, and the goal is to map a position to its corresponding value in the base pattern.

general_skills.title: Layered Operation Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break down multi-step processes into individual operations, calculating intermediate states by applying inverse transformations step-by-step from the final target.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When resolving problems with nested or sequential operations that require reverse-engineering from the final state to the initial conditions.

general_skills.title: Compute Outlier Thresholds
general_skills.principle: Calculate lower and upper bounds for outliers using the interquartile range (IQR) and the 1.5×IQR rule: lower bound = Q1 - 1.5×IQR, upper bound = Q3 + 1.5×IQR.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given quartiles (Q1, Q3) and required to determine outlier thresholds.

general_skills.title: Check Data Points Against Bounds
general_skills.principle: Systematically compare each data point to the computed outlier thresholds to identify values below the lower bound or above the upper bound.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing a dataset to count outliers based on predefined statistical thresholds.

general_skills.title: Apply Quartile-Based Definitions
general_skills.principle: Use provided quartiles (Q1, Q3) to compute the interquartile range (IQR) and apply the outlier definition based on the 1.5×IQR rule.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems that require outlier detection using quartile statistics.

general_skills.title: Model Geometric Constraints with Coordinates
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to key points based on given constraints (e.g., tangency, diameters) to simplify spatial relationships and calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves multiple circles or shapes with specific tangency or alignment conditions.

general_skills.title: Decompose Complex Areas into Standard Components
general_skills.principle: Break down irregular regions (e.g., lens-shaped intersections) into sectors, triangles, or other standard shapes to compute their areas systematically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating areas of overlap or shaded regions in geometric configurations involving circles or polygons.

general_skills.title: Apply Geometric Relations to Determine Positions
general_skills.principle: Use properties like tangency, diameters, or symmetry to infer distances or positions of centers, enabling precise area calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems requiring the placement of circles or points based on given geometric constraints.

general_skills.title: Generate Initial Terms for Pattern Recognition
general_skills.principle: Compute early terms of a sequence to identify structural patterns or constraints that limit possible solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing recursive sequences to detect periodicity, growth trends, or contradictions.

general_skills.title: Modular Arithmetic for Contradiction Detection
general_skills.principle: Use modular constraints (e.g., mod 3, 4, 5) to eliminate cases where a term could be a perfect square.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying whether a sequence term can satisfy properties of squares or other number-theoretic conditions.

general_skills.title: Bounding Expressions Between Consecutive Squares
general_skills.principle: Analyze the gap between consecutive squares to determine if a term can lie within that range, thereby ruling out square possibilities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When assessing whether a sequence term can be a perfect square by comparing it to known square bounds.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Translate geometric configurations into coordinate systems to compute distances and relationships between points.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves geometric figures with proportional divisions or parallel segments.

general_skills.title: Arithmetic Series Summation
general_skills.principle: Use summation formulas for arithmetic sequences to compute total lengths of parallel or linearly varying segments.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires summing lengths that form a linear pattern over discrete intervals.

general_skills.title: Proportional Division Analysis
general_skills.principle: Leverage proportional division of segments to identify linear relationships between positions and lengths.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves dividing sides into equal parts and calculating lengths based on their relative positions.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition via Small Cases
general_skills.principle: Test small instances of a problem to identify emergent patterns or relationships, which can then be generalized.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem's behavior is unclear, use small cases to uncover underlying structure or trends.

general_skills.title: Formula Generalization from Observations
general_skills.principle: Derive a mathematical formula or relationship from observed patterns, even if the initial pattern appears non-linear or complex.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a pattern is identified, abstract it into a concise formula to model the problem's behavior.

general_skills.title: Equation Solving from Derived Models
general_skills.principle: Use a mathematically derived formula to set up and solve equations for unknown variables in the problem.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a formula is established, apply it to solve for the target quantity by equating it to known constraints.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Distance Calculation
