general_skills.principle: Use the distance formula between two points to determine spatial relationships in coordinate geometry.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given coordinates of points in a geometric figure, compute distances to infer side lengths or other properties.

general_skills.title: Geometric Property Inference
general_skills.principle: Leverage known properties of regular polygons (e.g., vertex spacing, side-length ratios) to relate given distances to unknown parameters.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing regular polygons, use established geometric relationships to connect vertex positions to side lengths or angles.

general_skills.title: Formula Substitution for Area
general_skills.principle: Apply standard area formulas for regular polygons (e.g., hexagon) after determining side lengths through geometric or coordinate analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Once side lengths are derived, substitute into area formulas to compute the target quantity in the required form.

general_skills.title: Vector Proportionality
general_skills.principle: When two vectors are parallel, their components are proportional. Use this relationship to set up equations between known and unknown components.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given a direction vector with an unknown component and a known direction, use proportionality to relate the components.

general_skills.title: Geometric Configuration Analysis
general_skills.principle: Derive equations from geometric relationships by identifying key points, lines, or vectors in the problem setup.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a diagram or coordinate system provides explicit geometric relationships (e.g., points, lines, or direction vectors).

general_skills.title: Proportional Equation Solving
general_skills.principle: Solve for unknowns in proportional relationships by cross-multiplying and simplifying ratios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an unknown variable is part of a proportion derived from parallel vectors or equivalent ratios.

general_skills.title: Model Remainder Constraints
general_skills.principle: Express quantities as a multiple of a base unit plus a remainder to capture conditions involving division and remainders.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem specifies a remainder after dividing by a certain value (e.g., quarters or dimes).

general_skills.title: Find Intersection of Solution Sets
general_skills.principle: Generate possible values for each constraint and identify their common elements to satisfy multiple conditions simultaneously.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple constraints must be satisfied by the same quantity (e.g., both quarter and dime-based remainder conditions).

general_skills.title: Verify Candidates Against All Conditions
general_skills.principle: Check each candidate solution against all original problem constraints to ensure consistency and correctness.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After identifying potential solutions, to confirm they meet all specified requirements.

general_skills.title: Model Circular Structures
general_skills.principle: Identify adjacency relationships in circular configurations and count pairs based on geometric constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing problems involving cyclic arrangements or adjacency-based interactions.

general_skills.title: Use Probability Distributions for Sums
general_skills.principle: Compute probabilities of sums from independent variables using known distributions (e.g., dice rolls).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating likelihoods of composite outcomes from independent random variables.

general_skills.title: Apply Linearity of Expectation
general_skills.principle: Decompose complex expectations into sums of individual probabilities for independent events.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating expected counts of overlapping or dependent events in combinatorial settings.

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Generation
general_skills.principle: When constraints define a set of possibilities, iterate through all valid combinations to ensure completeness, such as enumerating all (a, b) pairs where a + b = 15.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires exploring all possible values under specific constraints, like generating all special fractions in the problem.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification for Integer Conditions
general_skills.principle: Transform complex expressions into simpler forms by substituting variables and simplifying, enabling identification of conditions for integrality (e.g., analyzing the sum of two fractions as a function of their variables).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing sums or products of variables under constraints to determine when they satisfy specific properties like being integers.

general_skills.title: Distinct Outcome Deduplication
general_skills.principle: After generating all possible outcomes, filter and count unique values by systematically eliminating duplicates, ensuring each distinct result is considered only once.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating a set of results (e.g., sums of fractions) to determine the number of unique values that satisfy a condition.

general_skills.title: Count permutations with repeated elements
general_skills.principle: Calculate total distinct permutations by dividing factorial of total elements by product of factorials of repeated element counts.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the total number of unique arrangements of a multiset of characters.

general_skills.title: Case analysis for substring constraints
general_skills.principle: Split problems into cases based on the number of valid substring occurrences, adjusting for overlaps and overcounting.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing permutations with forbidden substrings or other combinatorial constraints requiring scenario-specific counting.

general_skills.title: Inclusion-exclusion for overlapping cases
general_skills.principle: Subtract overcounted scenarios by alternating addition and subtraction of overlapping cases to correct for double-counting.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When adjusting counts for overlapping invalid configurations in combinatorial problems.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Based Sum Bounding
general_skills.principle: Use average constraints to derive a maximum total sum, then narrow candidate sets to numbers within this bound while satisfying distinctness and range conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given an average constraint on a set of numbers with distinct values in a bounded range, calculate the maximum possible sum and use it to filter candidate combinations.

general_skills.title: LCM Prime Factor Analysis
general_skills.principle: Decompose the LCM into its prime factors to identify required prime components in the set, ensuring all numbers contribute to the LCM's factorization without introducing extraneous primes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing a set's LCM, factorize the LCM and use it to determine which numbers (and their prime components) must be included or excluded to meet the LCM requirement.

general_skills.title: Constraint Verification
general_skills.principle: Systematically check candidate solutions against all problem constraints (e.g., LCM, sum, distinctness) to confirm uniqueness and validity, eliminating alternatives that fail any condition.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying a solution's correctness, exhaustively test against all given constraints to ensure no alternative configurations satisfy the conditions.

general_skills.title: Hypergeometric Modeling
general_skills.principle: When selecting a subset from a larger set without replacement, model the expected count of a specific category using hypergeometric distribution parameters: population size, success states, and sample size.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves sampling without replacement and requires computing expected counts of a subset.

general_skills.title: Linearity of Expectation Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break down complex expectations into simpler components by focusing on relative positions or counts, then sum their contributions using linearity of expectation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating expected values for positions or counts that depend on multiple independent factors.

general_skills.title: Relative Position Analysis
general_skills.principle: The position of an element in a sorted row is determined by the number of elements less than it in that row, allowing translation of positional expectations into combinatorial counts.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing the relative ordering of elements in a structured grid or sequence.

general_skills.title: Constraint Verification
general_skills.principle: Systematically check each problem condition in sequence to ensure all constraints are met, starting with the most restrictive.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems with multiple interdependent constraints, such as digit restrictions and derived number properties.

general_skills.title: Incremental Testing
general_skills.principle: Test small numerical cases in ascending order to identify the minimal solution that satisfies all criteria.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When searching for the smallest value meeting specific properties, such as perfect squares with digit-based constraints.

general_skills.title: Truncation Manipulation
general_skills.principle: Apply mathematical operations like division or truncation to isolate segments of a number for verification.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When needing to check specific parts of a number (e.g., truncated digits) as required by the problem's conditions.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis via Element Distribution
general_skills.principle: Break down complex constraints into cases based on how elements are distributed among overlapping regions of sets, ensuring all constraints are satisfied in each case.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with problems involving multiple overlapping sets with specific intersection or size requirements.

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Counting for Region Partitions
general_skills.principle: Use combinatorial formulas (e.g., permutations, multinomial coefficients) to compute the number of ways to partition elements into distinct regions defined by set memberships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating configurations for cases that involve distributing elements into specific overlapping regions of sets.

general_skills.title: Constraint Validation in Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Verify that each case adheres to all problem constraints (e.g., set sizes, intersection sizes) by aligning computed distributions with the given conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When ensuring that each case in a case-based solution meets all required mathematical conditions.

general_skills.title: Decompose by Absolute Value Cases
general_skills.principle: Break the problem into cases based on the absolute value of the product, considering all integers k in the specified range.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves constraints on the absolute value of a product or expression.

general_skills.title: Count Divisor Pairs with Symmetry
general_skills.principle: For each integer k, count the number of ordered pairs (x, y) such that |xy| = k by considering positive/negative divisors and multiplying by 4 for each divisor pair.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting integer solutions to equations involving absolute values and products.

general_skills.title: Leverage Symmetry for Sign Variations
general_skills.principle: Account for positive and negative values by multiplying counts by 2 or 4, depending on the problem's symmetry constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires considering all sign combinations of variables or expressions.

general_skills.title: Categorize and Apply Value Based on Type
general_skills.principle: Identify elements as categories (e.g., prime/composite) and assign distinct values or operations to each category to compute contributions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires different actions or values based on inherent properties of elements (e.g., number types, geometric shapes).

general_skills.title: Compute Net Displacement via Weighted Sum
general_skills.principle: Calculate total effect by summing weighted contributions from each category, where weights correspond to problem-defined rules or transformations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining overall outcome from multiple distinct components with varying impacts (e.g., forces, scores, positional changes).

general_skills.title: Interpret Final Result as Absolute Magnitude
general_skills.principle: The required answer is the absolute value of the net result when the problem asks for return distance, magnitude, or equivalent measure.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem demands a non-negative measure of distance, magnitude, or corrective action based on directional displacement.

general_skills.title: State-Transition DP Modeling
general_skills.principle: Model path-counting problems using dynamic programming states that track current position and accumulated constraints, leveraging transitions between adjacent states to build solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires counting paths with cumulative constraints (e.g., sum, length) across a graph or grid.

general_skills.title: Recurrence-Based Subproblem Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break complex problems into subproblems via recurrence relations, where each state's value depends on adjacent states' values to compute cumulative possibilities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving combinatorial problems with overlapping subproblems, such as path counting or constraint satisfaction in graphs.

general_skills.title: Parity-Driven Compositeness Analysis
general_skills.principle: Use parity (even/odd) of expressions to infer compositeness. For example, if n is odd, p² + n is even for odd primes p, ensuring compositeness (except when the result is 2).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing expressions involving primes and a parameter n, leverage parity to simplify conditions and eliminate prime candidates.

general_skills.title: Case Splitting Based on Prime Properties
general_skills.principle: Split into cases (e.g., p=2 vs odd primes) to handle distinct scenarios. For example, separately verify conditions for the smallest prime (p=2) and general primes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving all primes, isolate special cases (like p=2) to address unique properties and ensure universal coverage.

general_skills.title: Minimal Value Verification
general_skills.principle: Test small values of the parameter (e.g., n=1, 3, 5) to confirm minimal validity. Check edge cases (like p=2) to rule out smaller candidates.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking the smallest solution, systematically test small values and validate against critical edge cases to ensure optimality.

general_skills.title: Apply Theorem-Based Proportions
general_skills.principle: Use geometric theorems (e.g., Angle Bisector Theorem) to derive proportional relationships between segments or sides in a figure, translating geometric constraints into algebraic equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves a geometric configuration with known ratios or bisectors, and integer or proportional relationships are implied.

general_skills.title: Enforce Integer Constraints via Scaling
general_skills.principle: Express side lengths as integer multiples of a variable (e.g., $ k $) derived from proportions, then determine valid integer values for the variable that satisfy all constraints (e.g., triangle inequalities).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When side lengths must be integers and proportional relationships are established, use scaling factors to generate candidate solutions.

general_skills.title: Systematic Triangle Inequality Verification
general_skills.principle: Check all triangle inequalities ($ a + b > c $) for derived side lengths to ensure the figure is nondegenerate, prioritizing the most restrictive inequality for minimal perimeter validation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After determining side lengths, verify triangle inequalities to confirm validity and exclude degenerate cases.

general_skills.title: Inclusion-Exclusion for Set Unions
general_skills.principle: To compute the size of the union of two sets, add their individual sizes and subtract the size of their intersection. This principle applies to any two sets defined by divisibility or other properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the count of elements satisfying 'A or B' in a finite universe.

general_skills.title: Set Difference via Intersection Subtraction
general_skills.principle: To exclude elements satisfying a third condition (e.g., 'not C'), subtract the intersection of the union with the forbidden set from the original union. This handles 'but not' constraints in combinatorial problems.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When requiring elements to satisfy a primary condition while excluding those that meet a secondary, conflicting condition.

general_skills.title: LCM-Based Overlap Calculation
general_skills.principle: The number of elements divisible by multiple numbers is determined by the least common multiple (LCM) of those numbers. Use floor division to count multiples within a range.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating overlaps between sets defined by divisibility or other periodic properties.

general_skills.title: Function Point Limitation
general_skills.principle: A function (e.g., quadratic) uniquely determined by a specific number of points can contribute at most that number of terms to a sequence, as additional points would redefine the function.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a function's uniqueness is tied to a specific number of input-output pairs in a sequence.

general_skills.title: Maximize Resource Utilization
general_skills.principle: To maximize the total number of terms, distribute the usage of available functions to their maximum capacity under the problem's constraints, ensuring no resource is underutilized.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When resources (e.g., functions) can be used multiple times but are limited by constraints such as uniqueness or structural requirements.

general_skills.title: Test Small Integer Values
general_skills.principle: Evaluate the target expression for small positive integers to identify potential solutions or eliminate impossible cases.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves a polynomial or function that is easy to compute for small inputs and the solution space is constrained.

general_skills.title: Check for Perfect Square Candidates
general_skills.principle: Directly verify if a computed value matches a perfect square by comparing it to known squares or algebraic identities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires determining if an expression evaluates to a square, especially after narrowing down candidate values.

general_skills.title: Analyze Growth Rates for Uniqueness
general_skills.principle: Assess the asymptotic behavior of the expression to determine if solutions are possible beyond small values, leveraging the relative growth rates of polynomials and squares.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing whether a function can yield a perfect square for large inputs, particularly when direct computation is infeasible.

general_skills.title: Recognize Algebraic Identities
general_skills.principle: Identify expressions as squares or other standard forms to simplify complex expressions under constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a quadratic or symmetric expression that can be rewritten as a known identity.

general_skills.title: Apply AM-GM Under Product Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use the AM-GM inequality to minimize sums given a product constraint, leveraging equality conditions when variables are equal.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing a sum under a product constraint, particularly when symmetry suggests equality in the variables.

general_skills.title: Leverage Symmetry in Optimization
general_skills.principle: Assume symmetry (e.g., equal variables) when equality in inequalities is required, ensuring constraints are satisfied.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When minimizing or maximizing expressions with symmetric constraints, and equality conditions are expected.

general_skills.title: Variable Substitution for System Reduction
general_skills.principle: Express one variable in terms of others to reduce the system's complexity, enabling direct substitution into remaining equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with a system of equations involving multiple variables, use substitution to decrease the number of variables and simplify the problem.

general_skills.title: Constraint Analysis via Non-Negative Terms
general_skills.principle: Recognize that equations involving sums of non-negative terms (e.g., squares) can only be satisfied if each term individually equals zero.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an equation reduces to a sum of non-negative terms equaling zero, conclude that each term must independently be zero.

general_skills.title: Simplify to Fundamental Forms
general_skills.principle: Transform complex equations into simpler forms (e.g., completing the square) to reveal inherent constraints or unique solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying equations, aim to convert them into standard forms (e.g., squares, linear expressions) that expose underlying structural properties.

general_skills.title: Decompose into Sequential Segments
general_skills.principle: When a path can be broken into independent segments, compute the number of ways for each segment and multiply them to find total possibilities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves sequential steps with independent choices at each stage.

general_skills.title: Enumerate All Intermediate Paths
general_skills.principle: Systematically identify all possible routes through intermediate nodes, considering direct and indirect connections, and sum their contributions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires accounting for multiple paths through intermediate points or nodes.

general_skills.title: Domain Restriction via Function Range
general_skills.principle: Identify constraints on variables by leveraging the bounded nature of functions (e.g., sine's range [-1, 1]) to narrow the search space for solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an equation involves a bounded function and a variable-term, use the function's range to restrict the domain of the variable.

general_skills.title: Periodic Interval Partitioning
general_skills.principle: Divide a domain into subintervals based on the period of a function to analyze intersections or behaviors within each cycle.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing periodic functions (e.g., sine) in equations, partition the domain into intervals corresponding to the function's period for systematic analysis.

general_skills.title: Symmetry-Based Solution Counting
general_skills.principle: Leverage symmetry (e.g., even/odd functions) to deduce solution counts on symmetric intervals, adjusting for overlaps at critical points.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving equations with symmetric properties, use mirrored intervals to simplify counting while accounting for overlapping solutions.

general_skills.title: Structure Permutations via Grouping
general_skills.principle: When avoiding palindromic substrings, group identical elements into non-overlapping pairs to prevent adjacent duplicates and longer palindromic patterns.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints require avoiding repeated patterns, decompose the problem into structured arrangements that inherently satisfy the constraints.

general_skills.title: Systematic Constraint Verification
general_skills.principle: Validate permutations by exhaustively checking all possible substrings for forbidden patterns, ensuring no palindromic configurations of length ≥2 exist.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying the validity of a permutation under multiple constraints, systematically test all substrings for compliance.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Assignment for Geometric Figures
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to vertices of shapes to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations, enabling precise calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves geometric figures with unknown positions or constraints.

general_skills.title: Tangency and Perpendicularity Relationships
general_skills.principle: Use the property that a tangent line is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact to derive constraints between points and lines.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a circle is tangent to a line or another circle, and the radius or tangent line's direction is known.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Distance and Equation Solving
general_skills.principle: Apply the distance formula and algebraic manipulation to solve for unknowns derived from geometric constraints, such as circle equations or coordinate relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for lengths, coordinates, or parameters in problems involving circles, lines, or polygons.

common_mistakes.description: Failing to verify that the final answer matches the problem's required format (actual year vs. number of years).
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The solver correctly calculated the number of years (28) but overlooked that the problem asks for the specific year, not the duration between events.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always confirm that the final answer aligns with the problem's question. If the question asks for a year, ensure the answer is the actual year, not a derived number of years.

common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The solver's logic assumed all 28-year spans would include valid leap years, but century years (e.g., 2100) may not be leap years, potentially invalidating the calculation.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Explicitly verify that the calculated span does not include century years not divisible by 400, as these are not leap years.

common_mistakes.description: Overlooking the cyclical nature of days of the week without accounting for full 7-year cycles.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The solver used a 4-year cycle (5 days shift) but failed to recognize that 7 such cycles (28 years) are needed to realign the day of the week, which is a critical step in the modular arithmetic approach.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always validate that the solution satisfies the modular equation (e.g., 5k ≡ 0 mod 7) and ensure the derived value is the smallest positive integer that meets the condition.

common_mistakes.description: Failing to verify the correctness of a derived solution against the original problem's constraints.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The solver accepted an algebraically valid intermediate result without confirming it satisfies the problem's requirements, leading to a contradiction with the ground truth.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always validate the final answer by plugging it back into the original problem and ensuring it meets all stated conditions, especially when the problem involves multiple steps or hidden constraints.

common_mistakes.description: Overlooking multiple solutions in parametric equations (e.g., Pell equations) and stopping at the first apparent solution.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The solver focused on the immediate solution of a Pell-type equation without considering that higher-order solutions might be required to satisfy the problem's minimality condition.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Systematically explore all possible solutions of parametric equations, especially when the problem requires the smallest or largest value, and verify that the solution aligns with the problem's specific constraints.

common_mistakes.description: Misinterpreting coprimality or factorization in composite expressions, leading to incomplete case analysis.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The solver assumed a specific factorization of the product (n+1)(2n+1) without considering that coprimality might restrict valid factorizations, missing alternative cases that could yield correct solutions.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: When decomposing products into factors, rigorously analyze all possible coprime factorizations and ensure that each case is explored to avoid missing valid solutions.

common_mistakes.description: Assuming the existence of a valid sequence without verifying the second condition.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The agent concluded that 2M = 730 satisfies the second condition without checking whether any 6 consecutive integers squared sum to 730, leading to an incorrect final answer.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always rigorously verify that the derived value of 2M can indeed be expressed as the sum of 2n consecutive squares, even if the initial algebraic steps suggest it might be possible.

common_mistakes.description: Overlooking the necessity of checking all possible sequences for the second condition.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The agent focused on a specific sequence (e.g., starting at 10) without exhaustively checking if any other sequence of 2n integers could satisfy the sum, leading to a false positive.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Systematically test multiple starting points or use algebraic methods to confirm the existence of a valid sequence for the second condition, rather than relying on intuition alone.

common_mistakes.description: Incorrectly applying the angle bisector theorem by assuming D lies on EC instead of AC, leading to invalid segment ratios.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The angle bisector theorem requires the bisector to intersect the opposite side of the triangle. Since D is on AC, not EC, the theorem cannot be directly applied to triangle EBC, resulting in flawed segment ratios.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the angle bisector intersects the correct side of the triangle. When D is on AC, ensure calculations involve segments along AC, not EC.

common_mistakes.description: Failing to validate the final answer against the problem's constraints, such as given lengths and geometric relationships.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Overconfidence in intermediate steps can lead to overlooking contradictions with the problem's conditions, such as AC = 35 or BE = 5.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: After deriving a solution, explicitly check that all given values (e.g., BE = 5, AC = 35) are consistent with the final answer and geometric constraints.

common_mistakes.description: Incorrectly identifying divisors of the total number of solutions T, leading to invalid k values.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The user assumed numbers like 4, 5, 10, and 20 divide T = 2019 × 1009, but T is odd (product of two odd numbers), so even numbers like 4, 10, and 20 cannot divide it. This error stems from failing to verify divisibility of candidate divisors against the actual prime factorization of T.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always explicitly check whether a candidate divisor divides T by factoring T completely and ensuring the candidate is a product of its prime factors. Avoid assuming divisibility without verification.

common_mistakes.description: Misapplying the logic that (k + 1) divides f(k) implies f(k) must be a multiple of (k + 1).
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The user incorrectly assumed that f(k) equals T (total solutions) without accounting for the constraints, leading to an invalid assumption that f(k) is directly tied to T's divisors. This ignores the possibility that f(k) could be smaller or have different properties.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Clearly define f(k) as the total solutions minus invalid cases, and ensure that the logic connecting f(k) to T's divisors is rigorously validated. Avoid conflating f(k) with T without proper derivation.

common_mistakes.description: Incorrectly concluding the final answer without verifying against the problem's conditions.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The solver assumed n=1 and n=3 were valid solutions based on partial analysis but failed to confirm that these n's satisfy the condition for all k, leading to an invalid conclusion.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always cross-validate final answers against the problem's requirements, especially for universal quantifiers like 'for every positive integer k'.

common_mistakes.description: Misinterpreting the problem's formatting requirements for the final answer.

common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Carefully parse the problem's instructions for answer formatting and ensure the final answer aligns with the exact question phrasing, not assumptions.

common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Systematically test all critical cases (e.g., small k values) and ensure the solution holds universally, not just for observed examples.

common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Before finalizing an answer, ensure it matches the problem's requirements and use multiple independent methods (e.g., invariant analysis, case examples) to validate the result.

common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: For each number, explicitly list all possible multiples/divisors within the range and test all combinations, even if they conflict with initial assumptions about pairings.

common_mistakes.description: Incorrect evaluation of the infinite sum due to errors in partial fraction decomposition or telescoping series steps.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Failure to properly simplify the general term or miscalculating the telescoping sum leads to an incorrect value for the series, which propagates through subsequent steps.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Carefully verify each algebraic step, especially factoring and partial fraction decomposition, and validate the telescoping sum by testing partial sums or alternative methods.

common_mistakes.description: Incorrectly assuming the final form of the sum without verifying compatibility with the problem's constraints.

common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the problem's constraints (e.g., swap restrictions) are explicitly accounted for in the mathematical model, not just general permutation properties.
